content: Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting Minutes April 13, 2022, Minutes The Centre at University Park Attendance: Ren Bressinck, Matt Buie, Samuel Ellis, Ashley Martinez, Lauren Eldridge, and Linda Smith Absent: Alexandria Washington, Delwin Slater, Demetria Murdock, Doris Wright, Jesse Gibson, and Kenneth Taylor City Board of Director Liaison: Director Capi Peck LRPR Staff: City Attorney Beth Carpenter, Leland Couch, Angela Nelson, Shawanda Robinson, J.P Rogers and Kaleb Turner. Welcome and Introductions: Chairman Buie called the meeting to order and welcomed everyone present. Chairman Buie proceeded with the agenda to the roll call and approval of March's minutes. Roll Call and Approval of Minutes: Angela Nelson called the roll and Chairman Buie reported a quorum was four (4) members in attendance. Official business will be voted on during the meeting. Chairman Buie then entertained a motion to approve the March commission meeting minutes. Beth Carpenter mentioned on page three, paragraph five of the March minutes, which revisions should be made on the FOIA statement. Motion was moved by Commissioner Martinez. Seconded by Commissioner Eldridge. The March commission meeting minutes were approved. Citizen Communication: No citizen communication. Chairman Buie then called for any staff reports. Staff Reports: Director Leland Couch started staff reports by introducing J.P Rogers as the new Parks Maintenance Manager, who was at First Tee prior to accepting his new position. Director Couch also reintroduced Shawanda Robinson as the new Deputy Director of Recreation Services. Administration Angela Nelson Deputy Director of Administration proceeded with staff reports for Administration stating, staff at the front desk are taking reservations for pavilions and have noticed an increase in rentals since the opening of rental reservations. Nelson mentions that reservations are at 95% booked. She mentions the focus on receiving small training of reconciling and data entries that deal with the ActiveNet System the department uses. Nelson states that hiring is the top priority, getting all available positions filled. Lastly, Angela congratulated staff J.P Rogers and Shawanda Robinson on their new positions with the department. Recreation Deputy Director of Recreation Services, Shawanda Robinson opened recreation staff reports by informing the commission that there will be a Tennis Tournament March the 23rd-25th for the National level junior's Tournament. Following that tournament at the end of the month, there will be another tennis Tournament on the 29th-30th for the Chenal Junior's Tournament. Robinson mentions, there will be players coming from all the country to participate in these tournaments. Robinson then reported First Tee had a successful tournament over the weekend, with many of participants in attendance. Shawanda Robinson informs the commission that the Athletics Department, is preparing to start the Summer Playground Program on June 6th, which will occur for eight weeks. Registration for the program starts on May. Robinson mentions that numbers are being cut back in this program due to future concerns of Covid-19. Senior Programs are aging and active daily from various activities, such as their favorite, Bean Bag Baseball and Chair Volleyball. Deputy Director of Recreation Services, Shawanda Robinson reported that there was a Bean Bag Baseball tournament held at the West Central Community Center against other senior programs in the surrounding area. Shawanda Robinson lastly reported that all six community centers are gearing up for Soccer, Tee ball, and Baseball, starting on May 2nd. The Track and field program has been adjusted to accepting three and four year olds to play. MacArthur Museum is back open and doing school tours. Robinson lastly informed the commission that recreation will be creating new programs and activities for all ages, and calling them opportunities and experiences. Robinson mentioned programs like aviation, coding, and archery are ideas in the works for creating various opportunities and experiences in recreation. Parks Guest New Parks Maintenance Manager, J.P Rogers, introduced himself stating his experience of working 19 years with the City of Little Rock. Prior to joining the City of Little Rock, he worked in private sectors, public golf courses, and country clubs. Rogers mentions that in the past he has worked at (6) six golf courses. Rogers reports that currently he is taking care of First Tee and parks maintenance. Director Leland Couch mentions, he will proceed with his staff report during New Business on the topic of the Parks 2022 Budget. With no further reports, Chairman Buie proceeded to move down the agenda to old business. Old Business: Commissioner Lauren Eldridge gave an update on the 2022 Parks Commission Golf Tournament. Eldridge stated the official day of the Tournament will be the Friday before Memorial Day, May 27th staring at 8:00 AM. Lauren Eldridge mentioned that she has finalized an information packet, which she will be sending out. Commissioner Eldridge stated the tournament will be raising the prices on sponsorships this year, so there can be more money made, to go towards the beneficiary. As we move towards the start date of the tournament, Commissioner Eldridge states that prizes and raffle donations are needed. One prize mentioned from Commissioner Eldridge was a weekend at Oaklawn, presented by George at Rebsamen. On the day of the tournament Eldridge mentions that it would be helpful to have a couple of volunteers in the morning, to assist with on-site payment, getting beverages cold, and handing out goodies and information. Flight one will start at 8:00 AM and volunteers would need to report by 7:00- 7:15 AM. Flight two will start at 1:00 PM, after lunch that will be provided by Director Peck, Trios, and Chester's Chicken. Commissioner Eldridge continues to mention that the prizes and raffles will start at the end of the tournament. Commissioner Eldridge mentioned that Director Leland Couch will be creating a new and improved flyer to advertise registration and information of the 2022 Golf Tournament. Commissioner Eldridge ends her update by mentioning a one-way email being sent out to the commission about the Golf Tournament and updates. Chairman Buie asked for a reminder when time comes on volunteer assistance for the tournament. Lastly, Commissioner Eldridge stated that last year the proceeds went towards Wakefield Park for improvements, and this year's proceeds will create a fund for the kid's recreational programs that are offered by the Parks and Recreation Department. Chairman Buie steps in the conversation to formalize a vote to allow the proceeds from the Golf tournament to go into a special recreation fund that can be used by Deputy Director of Recreation Services Shawanda Robinson for recreational purposes. In Order to use funds, Robinson would come to the commission and request expenditure of funds through the account. The commission will then have the ability to vote on the recommended request. Chairman Buie then entertained a motion to approve the proceeds of the Golf Tournament going into a special funds account for recreational use. Motion was moved by Commissioner Eldridge and Seconded by Commissioner Ellis. The motion was approved. Director Couch questions Commissioner Eldridge if a Banner was ever used to advertise the tournament. Commissioner Eldridge responds saying that flyers in the center were available but a banner has never been used. Chairman Buie then proceeds to appointment of Committees. Chairman Buie restates chairs of each committee being: Parks Conservancy Liaison is Commissioner Bressinck, Outreach and Social Media, is Commissioner Martinez, and Master Plan and Vision, is Commissioner Smith. Chairman Buie asks Commissioner Martinez if there she has any questions or concerns and if she would like to appoint/ ask a couple of members of the commission to be a part of her respected committee. Chairman Buie tables the appointment of committees due to missing commissioners. Buie states that appointments will be held during next month's meeting. Also, Chairman Buie mentions that Director Couch has communicated with the City Clerk's office for replacements of members, three members have been appointed to the commission, who hopefully will be in attendance during May's Commission meeting. Chairman Buie then proceeds to New Business. New Business: Chairman Buie opens discussion on Parks 2022 Budget and gave the floor to Director Couch. Director Couch reported an update stating the first page of the budget is showing city information towards funding for previous sales tax, which is expired. The second page shows finalized projects intended for the years. Kanis parks improvements were towards the basketball courts and road infrastructure. Couch mentions there has been a final bid that project at $1.4 million. Interstate park improvements are towards the resurfacing of roadways. This project was at 60% moving to 90% in the engineering drawing, Couch plans on meeting with the engineering team to discuss the drawings. Boyle Park mountain biking was a grant the department received, which had a bid last year, then ran into some problems in the attorneys office, and now resolving those issues and close the bid. Western Hill is in the process of finishing project and Tri-Creek Greenway received $3 million in grants, along with Parks matching $750,000, making it a $3.7 million project. With no further discussion, Chairman Buie opened the floor for agenda items for next month's meeting. Lauren Eldridge comments on having the 2022 Golf Tournament added to the agenda for more updates. Director Leland Couch mentioned adding an update on Parks accreditation process. Chairman Buie lastly added to the commission, when new recruits are known and information is given, Buie encourages current Commissioners to reach out to them for welcoming. With no further discussion Chairman Buie adjourned the meeting at 1:02 p.m. The meeting was adjourned.

Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting Minutes May 18, 2022 The Centre at University Park Attendance: Matt Buie, Ashley Martinez, Lauren Eldridge, and Linda Smith (Virtual), Abby Jennings (Virtual), Cannon Fletcher Absent: Demetria Murdock, Director Doris Wright, Ren Bressinck, Samuel Ellis City Board of Director Liaison: Director Capi Peck LRPR Staff: City Attorney Beth Carpenter, Leland Couch, Angela Nelson, Shawanda Robinson, and Ricardo Ante. Welcome and Introductions: Chairman Buie called the meeting to order and welcomed everyone present. Chairman Buie proceeded with the agenda to the roll call and approval of April's minutes. Roll Call and Approval of Minutes: Angela Nelson called the roll and Chairman Buie reported a quorum was six (6) members (four in person and two virtual) in attendance. Official business will be voted on during the meeting. Chairman Buie then entertained a motion to approve the April's commission meeting minutes. Ashley Martinez mentioned on page one, paragraph one of the April's minutes, which revisions should be made on the quorum statement regarding attendance. Motion was moved by Commissioner Martinez. Seconded by Commissioner Eldridge. The April commission meeting minutes were approved. Citizen Communication: No citizen communication. Chairman Buie then called for any staff reports. Staff Reports: Director Leland Couch started staff reports by mentioning that he was filling in for the Deputy Director of Operations, and mentioned that the department had new hires in all those positions. Kanis Park would be getting a new set of basketball courts in a $1.5 million project. They include three (3) full courts and one (1) half-court, as well as a new entrance and trail systems. Director Couch mentioned that he was looking for the Board of Directors to approve a new part to the new playground, being built as all-inclusive, in the coming weeks. This will grow the site to over $1 million. Regarding maintenance, the department has also attained three (3) new contracts. The look of the parks were brought up and how they weren't being attended to as needed. This is due to staffing contracts expiring in March and they are negotiating these terms to take to the board. Lastly, the Western Hills playground was mentioned. The $1.5 million project would start on the playground, pavilion, the parking lot and trails later in the year. This would come from last year's tax campaign. He mentioned several other projects, but not by name due to time constraints. Director Couch gave way to questions, but none were asked at the time. Administration Deputy Director of Administration, Angela Nelson reported no updates. Recreation Deputy Director of Recreation Services, Shawanda Robinson opened recreation staff reports by informing the upcoming Summer Playground Program, starting June 6, 2022. She informed the Commission that the Athletics Department is preparing to start the Summer Playground Program on June 6th and will go on until July 21st. Registration for the program started on May 1st. Robinson mentions that numbers are being cut back in this program due to future concerns of Covid-19, with 210 at Dunbar, and 120 at others sites. Deputy Director Robinson mentioned that Tee-Ball, Junior Hoops and Summer League were starting practices, which is all done at Dunbar Community Center. She mentioned the 30-40 year old league is doing the same, with the culmination of years added up to forty-five (45). She stated how they were getting the program ready so that the children would be happy and have as much fun as possible this summer. The golf courses was the next topic, with several up coming tournaments. Therapeutic Recreation Division was the next topic, with their summer camp dates starting on the 6th of June as well. They are at full capacity in the division. Pool openings were the next topic. Southwest Community Center and Jim Dailey Fitness Centers are getting ready to open. An event has been scheduled, known as $1 Day on May 28, 2022. Deputy Director Robinson reported that there would be a Fitness in the Park at War Memorial Park; it will be an outside fitness day. MacArthur Military Museum will be having a Gold Star Family Picnic and Concert on June 12, 2022 at 7:00 p.m. The location will be outside by the pavilion. This concludes the Recreation Division. Deputy Director Robinson gave room for questions, but none were asked at this time. With no further reports, Chairman Buie proceeded to move down the agenda to old business. Old Business: Commissioner Lauren Eldridge gave an update on the 2022 Parks Commission Golf Tournament. Eldridge stated the official day of the Tournament will be the Friday before Memorial Day, May 27th staring at 8:00 am, Commissioner Eldridge mentioned that help is needed to spread the word and more to register for the event. She mentioned she was on The Buzz radio station earlier that morning, and will be on KARK next week promoting it as well. Commissioner Eldridge stated that she would need help from around 7:00 a.m. until the event shut down and that much help would be needed with passing out bags and taking payments since most people would be making payments day of the event. Commissioner Eldridge brought flyers for the event to pass along, as well as sending them in a PDF format for those attending virtually. Commissioner Eldridge stated the tournament will be giving out really fun prizes from around the city just to highlight the city. She said that E-Z-Go would be putting a golf cart at a hole, so that if you happen to make a hole-in-one, you win that golf cart. She mention that the 3 to 5 year outlook was to increase the awareness of it, and put the city on the map. One of the biggest things to the radio station was free drinks, compared to the PGA's $18 price tag on drinks. She mentioned again that the proceeds would be used for the Summer Opportunity and they would try to create a fund the Summer Playground Program could use at the committee's discretion. Plans are still being drawn out. Commissioner Eldridge requested that any questions regarding this event go to her, and in the case of interested ones, the information was on the flyer, yet she mentioned being emailed since she was putting together a list of those who are signing up. Chairman Buie thank Commissioner Eldridge for all of her hard work on this event, asked for a reminder when time comes on volunteer assistance for the tournament. He asked to plan to stay out there as long as possible. The Lauren team is partnering with City Parks Conservancy to take electronic payments as well. Commissioner Eldridge stated that there were two options for payment: check payment sent to Little Rock Parks and Recreation, payment on the day of the tournament, and cash would be accepted. Chairman Buie asked about word-of-mouth in terms of getting the word out about the event. In the case of getting registries, Commissioner Eldridge emphasized sponsorships are very affordable for this tournament and how the small businesses could put a sign on the course at a particular hole for $250 or for $500 a GPS location (logo on the GPS) on the golf cart for thirty (30) days and a sponsorship. It also comes with the possibility of a team registration if someone wants to add a team, with no extra cost if you want to become a $500 sponsor. She encourages anyone with connections to the local businesses to just reach out to get your name out there and to mention it's for the kids. Chairman Buie then states that at the last meeting, a vote was taken that Recreation will be the recipient of the funds from the tournament and at the appropriate time once the monies are there, then Shawanda would ask for the money to be delegated to a certain program. Chairman Buie opened the floor for comments to Commissioner Eldridge, yet none were given at the time. Then restated the need for volunteers at the event with Commissioner Eldridge. The Appointment of Committees were next on the agenda. Buie states that appointments will be held during this month's meeting. Chairman Buie restates chairs of each committee: Parks Conservancy Liaison is Commissioner Bressinck, whom being absent, could not appoint anyone to be on the committee. The next is Outreach and Social Media, and Commissioner Martinez reports no updates, but asks for anyone that would like to join to let her know. She mentioned taking volunteers to establish those committees, to with the chairman agreed. Chairman Buie mentioned how since there were only six (6) of the ten (10) members available, some would have to pull double duty if they decided to sign up for any number of Commissions or sub-committees. He then brings Commissioners Fletcher and Jennings up to speed, and asks if they had gotten a copy of the Commission Bylaws, and informs them to let someone know if they do not have a copy. The purpose of these committees is to have meaningful interaction with the staff on these three points, and to assist staff with furthering those particular initiatives. The next committee was Master Plan & Vision, chaired by Commissioner L. Smith. She reports no updates. She mentioned reaching out to a couple of others and will have finalized plans by the next meeting. Commissioner Smith stated that Commissioner Dustin Smith was out of the state on vacation, giving that as the reason for his absence, and mentioned that she was happy he became a part of the Commission, yet they are not related. To that remark, Attorney Carpenter states that the bylaws mention that the chairs of those committees would have to appoint the Commissioners to their committees as members. She states that it would have to be approved by the entire Commission. The Chairman then asked if any of the committee chairs have reached out to the member. Commissioner Martinez states that she had not because she didn't think that she was allowed to reach out. Attorney Carpenter says, reaching out outside of the meeting is a little (inaudible) you might not want to do that. To this, they make the necessary appointments the members at the meeting. Chairman Buie asks if anyone would like to join these committees, to which there are. Commissioner Eldridge joins Commissioner Martinez on the Outreach & Social Media. Commissioners Jennings, Ellis, and D. Smith join Commissioner L. Smith on Master Plans & Visions. It was mentioned that updates would be given every month to see the progress that these committees have made. Commissioner Martinez moved for the motion to be approved, and Commissioner Eldridge seconded it. The motion was approved by the Commission. Director Couch asks Attorney Carpenter about meeting with the other committees, to which she stated that the meetings would have to be publicized, and the social media outlets would have to be notified at least 2 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. She mentioned contacting Spencer Watson to notify the media, and Little Rock Parks and Recreation for building usage. She also mentioned using some time before, which previous Commissions did. Commissioner Martinez asked about the taking of minutes during those meetings, to which Attorney stated that since the meetings were open, minutes must be taken. It was stated that meetings must be recorded, either in video or audio format. Then proceeds to New Business. New Business: Chairman Buie opens discussion on the three (3) new Commission Members: Abby Jennings, Cannon Fletcher, and Dustin Smith. Chairman Buie gave the floor over to Commissioner Fletcher for him to tell about himself. Next, Commissioner Jennings was given the floor to tell about herself. The chairman mentioned that with the addition of three new members, there was still room for one or two more. With no further discussion, Chairman Buie opened the floor to Karen Sykes, for a presentation. Presentation Karen Sykes, The Park Ranger/Volunteer Programs Coordinator, introduced herself informing the Commission she has been in her position for a total of seven (7) years. First on the list was a past event, the MacArthur 5K race, where her team won the Corporate Cup, and she came in for her age division. The next event was Music in the Park, 4:00 pm - 7:30 pm which is taking place on June 3rd. Sykes mentioned there is a need for volunteers. There is also an event on October 6th at Allsopp Park at 5:00 pm as a two-part series. This event coincides with Hillcrest Day, which is on the first (1st) Thursday of each month. Sykes mentioned her programs are not part of the general budget so she has created fundraisers like Music in the Park. While doing this, she has increased the number of parks adopted, as well as the number of volunteerism for the city which has increased by 44% . This means providing funds for volunteers to make the parks beautiful; purchasing tools, flowers, grabbers and including water and snacks if possible. She also mentioned bringing back the banquet for volunteers in the fall, if permitted. Next, Karen states Music in the Park is a field of festivals with vendors. It is food trucks, beer vendors, and it is two bands on one stage (The On-Call band and Sad Daddy band). She mentioned there is a special outreach to non-profits to connect and grow memberships, grow volunteerism and branding and help each other. The deadline for the thirty-five (35) vendors was May 19th with all payments due May 25th. There will be a VIP tent with food and beverages. She informed the Commission that the event is free to the public as well. With no further discussion, Chairman Buie opened the floor for agenda items for next month's meeting. City Director, Capi Peck made a recommendation to talk about an effort to promote the bond issue passed at the Board meeting last night, to the agenda. Parks Director, Leland Couch mentioned adding two (2) updates. First, is introducing a social event during the year at half year for the Commission that will be more casual where we can get together to know each other better, as well as understand. We can bring up and finalize a date/ time and organize it. Second, introducing new Parks and Recreation staff for presentations. However, this will not need a vote and it will be a standing agenda item. Chairman Buie yielded the floor to Director Peck for City Liaison feedback, who reinforced the need to fill any vacancies on the committee, and mentioned that all local city boards and commissions are struggling right now and for no one to become discouraged because lack of attendance, because of the pandemic and the option to attend virtual. We are not the only ones. It's city wide, so don't feel like we are not loved and important. It's happening everywhere. City Director Peck stated she is anxious to get an energized group back and welcomed Commissioner Martinez to her second meeting. She also congratulated Parks Director, Leland Couch on becoming the Director. Peck asked about about vacancies which Commissioner Buie mentioned there may be one or two vacancies, but will need to reference attendance. Director Peck mentioned the bond issue and put forth some facts about it; it helps to get more money for infrastructure, for trails and for parks. The Board approved to be on the ballot August 9th. She would like to see the 3/8th tax back on the ballot; It is critical we fund our Parks system. If we get it on the ballot, people will support it. She mentioned we all need to become cheerleaders to make sure that passes on August 9th. It was suggested by Director Couch, a letter from the Commission needs to be voted upon to send regarding this to the Board of Directors for the City of Little Rock. Deputy Director Shawanda Robinson mentioned through AARP each Commissioner sent a letter to the Board. City Attorney Beth Carpenter agreed that is an option as well. Also, Director Peck encouraged Commissioner Eldridge to give a report at a Board Meeting about the Golf Tournament and where the funds are being distributed. Commissioner Fletcher mentioned adding Tennis Centric (Arkansas Tennis Pro). It started May 30th at Rebsamen Tennis. It is minor tennis leagues and the only tournament of this size and an unique opportunity for a city of this size. He recommended everyone to attend. Commissioner Buie then asked and stated this was just a notification and not for an agenda item and thank him for the information. With no further discussion, Chairman Buie adjourned the meeting at 1:07 p.m. The meeting was adjourned.

Meeting Notice The Parks and Recreation Commission will hold its regular meeting at The Centre at University Park and virtually via WebEx at 12:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 8, 2022. Agenda 1. Welcome 2. Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting Minutes June 8, 2022, Minutes The Centre at University Park Attendance: Matt Buie, Ashley Martinez (Virtual), Linda Smith, Abby Jennings (Virtual), Cannon Fletcher, Director Doris Wright, Dustin Smith (Virtual), Samuel Ellis Absent: Lauren Eldridge, Ricardo Ante, Ren Bressinck, Demetria Murdock City Board of Director Liaison: Director Capi Peck LRPR Staff: City Attorney Beth Carpenter, Leland Couch, Angela Nelson, Shawanda Robinson, J.P. Rogers Welcome and Introductions: Chairman Buie called the meeting to order and welcomed everyone present. Chairman Buie proceeded with the agenda to the roll call and approval of March's minutes. Roll Call and Approval of Minutes: Deputy Director Angela Nelson called the roll and Chairman Buie reported a quorum was seven (7) members (four in person and three virtual) in attendance. Official business will be voted on during the meeting. Chairman Buie then entertained a motion to approve the May commission meeting minutes. The May commission meeting minutes were approved. Citizen Communication: No citizen communication. Chairman Buie then called for any staff reports. Staff Reports: Director Leland Couch started staff reports by mentioning that he was covering operations, and mentioned that Parks Maintenance Manager J. P. Rogers would cover a few points on maintenance. Director Couch spoke on operations, which included any construction projects that were going on. Many of these have been previously reported on in the past, so only updates were given. Kanis Park kickoff of the first pre-construction meeting is to take place next week. For MacArthur's all-inclusive playground, the Board approved another addition, a phase II to the project. He mentioned that it was very important to him to finish that project. Western Hills' playground was still under construction at the moment, and they were looking to purchase a pavilion and restroom to continue that project. Right now, staff and construction crew are working at Rebsamen Pro Shop, since there were some failures down in the outdoor deck area, and improvements needed to happen. A new treehouse was completed in Riverfront Park and a small grand opening will happen as soon as landscaping is complete. The Dunbar Community Garden is working on a new sculpture at the entrance, that will start later in the fall. West Central plans for an outdoor recreation center will be happening soon. After the crew finishes the construction at Rebsamen, they will start on a new pavilion at West Central. Director Couch also mentioned a new cargo container getting delivered to start on some improvements. Those were just some of the upcoming and ongoing projects happening. Director Couch gave way to questions, but none were asked at the time. Director Peck mentioned how she thought the new treehouse was very nice and that she enjoyed the view. Director Couch mentioned that the treehouse was right off the Arkansas River, and it was both developed and constructed by Parks staff. Director Couch yielded the floor to Commissioner Buie for staff reports. Administration Deputy Director of Administration, Angela Nelson, reported no updates. Recreation Deputy Director of Recreation Services, Shawanda Robinson reported the Summer Playground Program, started June 7, 2022. Dunbar, has two-hundred and five (205) children, forty (40) at East Little Rock Community Center, one-hundred and twenty (120) at Stephens, about twentyeight (28) at Watson, about twenty-six (26) at J.A. Fair (Teen Camp), and roughly thirty-five (35) at Romine. West Central Community Center has around one-hundred (100) children. She mentioned that she was looking forward to all of the fun activities that we have for the children at the Summer Programs and Camps. Director Wright asked the number of children at East Little Rock, and made a correction about West Central's summer program. Wright mentioned that West Central did not have a Summer Playground Program, but was a Summer STEAM program, funded by Esser Grant, not the city. Golf was the next topic. The Parks Commission Tournament was held on May 27th at Rebsamen Golf Course, but allowed Chairman Buie to speak more on that at a better time. Tennis was the next topic. Two tournaments just finished. Both turned out great at Rebsamen Tennis Facility. We had the Wild Card and Little Rock Tennis Pro tournaments, where there were both large turnouts. Deputy Director Robinson got the chance to go out and enjoy some activities. Therapeutics Recreation Division was the next topic, with their summer camp dates starting on the 6th of June as well. They have two locations, Ottenheimer Center and at War Memorial Pro Shop, where they will be until July 21st. Pool openings were the next topic. Jim Dailey had a pool party known as $1 Day on May 28, 2022. Over eighty (80) people attended, and there were giveaways and door prizes. They had live music, and refreshments. They will host The World's Largest Swim Lesson on the 23rd and asked the Commission to stop by and check it out. Fitness in the Parks date has changed to June 28th, along with a Movie night, and Robinson advised them to join in. Senior Programs was the next topic. They are busy doing their activities and programs as well as interacting with the children at those locations. They're doing their best to share the spaces Deputy Director Robinson gave room for questions, to which Director Wright stated she did. Director Wright asked about the sports aspect, to which Deputy Director Robinson spoke. Baseball was supposed to start on the 6th, but due to rain it was postponed. Director Wright asked about the number of teams, to which Deputy Director Robinson stated that there about thirty-five (35) to forty (40) teams. The category are three and four (3 & 4) year olds, five and six (5 & 6) year olds, seven and eight (7 & 8) year olds, and there are no twelve (12) year olds. The games will be played at West Central Community Center. Track, and soccer are both coming up. Basketball clinics are going on at Dunbar on Saturdays, and Volleyball clinics are happening on Sundays. Basketball numbers are slow, with only two (2) to five (5) kids showing up, on the 4th, but it was the first time they met. The volleyball clinic has about twenty-five (25) to thirty (30) kids showing up. With this, Deputy Director Robinson opened the floor to questions, but none were stated at the time. Parks Maintenance Parks Maintenance Manager, J.P. Rogers opened parks maintenance reports by mentioned that the Board approved the contracts for our thirty (30) parks, eight (8) community centers, and three (3) large parks (Riverfront, Allsopp, and MacArthur) the previous night. Contractors are already out, and hopefully things will be caught up. They have been coming in early to start, because between the weather and other aspects, they have gotten behind. To the internal crew, there are still fifteen (15) parks. Seven (7) people have been hired (four being full-time), yet there are still twenty-one (21) open vacancies, since CDL drivers are hard to find. At this point, some catching up is occurring, but other areas (i.e. parts of Hindman) are hard to access because of the environment, but the higher use areas are being cut, since they are drier. Rogers opened the floor to questions but none were asked at the time. Director Couch mentioned having a successful "Music in the Park" event on the previous Friday. It was a small event, and they look forward to other events. He was looking forward to a couple of different tournaments, and invited the committee to give any ideas they had. He mentioned the event in Allsopp will be in October. Director Peck asked for the approximate attendance, to which Director Couch stated there was no counting of people, since it was an outdoor public event, but roughly around three-hundred (300) attended. It started slowly, but picked up around 5:00 p.m., but around 7:00 p.m., it started to fall off. Money was raised for the volunteer services, and awareness was raised around Parks and Recreation. With no further reports, Chairman Buie proceeded to move down the agenda to old business. Old Business: Chairman Buie opened up new business by mentioning noting there were two additional items that needed to be discussed, to which City Attorney Carpenter mentioned sending out an amendment agenda ahead of time. He then asked the commission. The Commission welcomed three (3) new committee members: Abby Jennings, Cannon Fletcher and Dustin Smith. Chairman Buie then gave the floor over to Commissioner Dustin Smith, tell about himself. He then moved quickly to committee reports. Starting with the Master Plan & Vision committee, Commissioner Linda Smith stated, that they met the prior day, and all were in attendance (four (4) commissioners and staff), and the outcome was very worthwhile. The first thing that happened was the committee each got a copy of the Master Plan and Vision Book, which was adopted in 2020. They then looked at the Strategic Plan Book. Commissioner Smith stated that the Master Plan book was designed to be a ten (10) year document, and the Strategic Plan Book was designed to be a five (5) year document. Both of these books were reviewed, and they mentioned ways to share information better online as far as having them linked to the public access. They also talked about ways for the commissioners to take special interest in the parks they live in close proximity to. They will be meeting again, but did not set an exact date. Commissioner L. Smith mentioned possibly having quarterly meetings for that committee. She mentioned that attached to the Agenda, she asked Deputy Director Nelson to add two pages from the Master Plan. At this, the Parks Guest Mr. Mason Ellis, was invited up to speak more on Rose Creek. He is the brother of Commissioner Samuel Ellis. Director Couch stated that Rose Creek Park is not an actual city park, but Parks has maintained it, and has been working with the neighborhood to raise money for an update to the existing trail system. He mentioned that he asked Mr. Ellis to speak to allow him to give an opportunity to share his work in this location, and at the end of the day, Couch would like to make the park a formal city park. He stated that it was indeed Parks Property, yet it has not been covered on inventory. Parks Guest Mr. Mason Ellis stepped to the podium and introduce himself. Mr. Ellis stated that he was very passionate about the subject, and moved to the Stiff Station area about five (5) years ago. Ellis sits at the chair of the Rose Creek Park Initiative. As of last year, they have their 501�3, making them an official non-profit organization. As an organization they have held several events, including clean-ups, tours, and work-days. Next, he showed a map of Rose Creek, and gave its location. Ellis mentioned that the group has been around since 2010, and he has been involved since 2015. Even before this, there have been conversations about it, and the idea of a park has been around for over 100 years. It was first mentioned in 1912 by John Noland, famous landscaper who went around to different cities and did master plans, and how it could connect to several other places. The next slide shows the outline of the park. Since Ellis' time of the board, about fourteen (14) properties have been donated to the city for the purposes of the park. He stated that all of those properties were in a floodplain, so no home would be built unless a lot of work was done. Last year at the Keep Little Rock Beautiful clean-up event, they gave out a bunch of blank maps and then what they wanted to see in their neighborhood park. They got a variety of suggestions on this, including playground, Dog Park, disc golf, and train viewing platform. Earlier in the year, they had their first Rose Creek Pop-Up. The set up things, and even repurposed a goal into a basketball court. Parks and Recreation Re-Creation set up this event, and they got a taste of some of their own ideas. It rained most of the day, yet by noon, a lot of people came out. The next slide showed how McClellan Engineers were contracted to do a survey of the property, as well as preliminary drawings of what the park could look like. The following slide show one of the key aspects that the group works on, Rose Creek Trail. The goal is to connect with the Arkansas River Trail System. If that happens, Rose Creek will be the only single-family residential neighborhoods with direct access to the Arkansas River Trail System in Little Rock. Everywhere else has to either bike on city streets or load their bike on and go. The ultimate goal is to connect to both the Arkansas River Trail and the Southwest Trail, which goes to Hot Springs, from Seventh (7th) Street. It also serves as a crucial piece of the Midline, a system that goes from East to West along I-630. The next slide shows the annual Rose Creek Trail Hike. Every year, the last Saturday in February, the Rose Creek Initiative hosts a hike, starting at Central High School and goes about two (2) miles to the Arkansas River. Another event, the first Saturday in December, they host a Fireworks Watch Party when the Capital shoots off its Christmas fireworks. The last component that the Rose Creek Initiative is the Rose Creek Watershed. It's a 1500 acre watershed that doesn't flow into Fourche, it flows directly into the Arkansas River. This watershed starts at Knoop Park and rolls through hillcrest, under UAMS, down Plateau St, under I-630, and then follows the rail corridor to the Arkansas River. It encompasses Arkansas Children's Hospital, UAMS, Central Arkansas Water, State Capital Complex, Dillard's, the Episcopal School, and together hopefully they can create a storm water management program, to help decrease litter and increase water quality. Ellis mentioned that they took a walk with one of the neighbors, who is a biologist, and discovered mussels in the creek. Earlier in the year, they worked alongside Dr. John Vineski and implemented their own trash boon, to decrease the trash that was getting in the park. In the end, they want to get it to grow, and officially become a city park. Chairman Buie opened the floor for any discussion. An inaudible comment was given by Commissioner L. Smith. Director Couch then asked the Commission to vote in support of Rose Creek becoming an official city park, and asked Attorney Beth Carpenter if this was appropriate. Carpenter mentioned that the board serves as an advisory commission to the city board and the city manager, and it could vote to show support to Rose Creek Initiative in Rose Creek Park becoming a city park. It was moved by Commission Ellis, and seconded by Commissioner Smith. Chairman asked for any additional comments or questions before the vote took place, to which no one did. A vote was taken, and the ayes had it. A vote was given to take to the City Manager, in support of the Rose Creek Initiative so that Rose Creek Park would become an official city park. Attorney Carpenter mentioned that there may be other steps, once it goes before the City Manager. Director Couch stated that this was a formal representation from this Commission that the Commission supports this concept. He then thanked the Commission, and Ellis for giving his presentation. Chairman Buie restated that a unanimous vote from the seven members of the Commission moved forward the motion, moved by Commissioner Ellis and seconded by Commissioner Smith, down to the City Manager. Next on the list is the aforementioned social event. Director Couch stated that this was the continuation of the concept of everyone getting together as a Commission outside of these rooms, and getting to know everyone a little better. He stated that to make Attorney Carpenter be at ease, the event would be publicized and promoted. Hill Station was picked as the location, due to it working in the past. Couch mentioned waiting until October 21st. Chairman Buie asked for any questions regarding the location and date for the event, to which none were asked. Director Couch mentioned that he would be sending out more information regarding this, and Buie encouraged the other Commissioners to join them if not otherwise previously engaged. The next item on the agenda is to add items to the next meeting agenda. He mentioned that the agenda was pretty well set, with citizen communication, staff reports, old business, new business (which deals with all aspects of sub-committees). He then stated that there would be a presentation from staff. Buie then asked if there were anything that needed to be added. Commissioner Jennings asked about the Friends of the Park program, and that she and Commission Smith spoke to Director Couch about that, and stated that she wanted to help in any way possible with this. She wanted to get the information ready by Harvest Fest. Chairman Buie then mentioned considering a partnership regarding this. Director Couch wanted to add Friends to the Park to the agenda, so that input and presentations could be given. He stated that another one that he would like to add was a presentation on the First Tee Complex, and there were some things that he wanted to address, and they had a new Facility Director there, who can come and introduce himself, as well as give some new ideas to the Commission. With no further discussion, the Commission turned to Board Liaison Feedback, with Director Wright. Director Wright started off by mentioning the second tranche of the American Rescue Plan Act. The board came up with the alternative to what was submitted to them, and they came forward with a resolution, but they pulled it back to not confuse the voters. They didn't want people to not vote for something based on the money that was going to them from the Act, and not to interfere with the August 8th millage. Right after the vote, Wright stated that she would be bringing back that resolution, and in it there are two allocation to Parks and Community Centers, and a dedicated Senior Center. To this affect, she stated that she would like the Parks department to begin more structure within the administration of our Parks Department for Senior Programming, and not let it be something that just takes place at community centers, because a dedicated center is going to need someone that understands how to interact and direct a facility, as well as programming for seniors. Wright mentioned that programming dollars are always an issue, due to staffing, so she just wanted to put that on the table, because the Board is going to have a dedicated Senior Center, and the goal is buy the old Carelink building, and to connect it via trails to both the Adult Center and Rebsamen Tennis Center. This would make it a Health and Wellness Center, not just a building. The Age-Friendly Little Rock Commission is working on a plan for that, but had no information on the next date. One of the things that they wanted was a pool for therapeutic use for seniors. Wright then mentioned that she wanted parks to think along those lines to giving some structure to it. She also mentioned giving updates to each Community Centers, taking care of maintenance and sprucing up the centers. She intends on having it presented to the board by the end of August. She stated that the funds are already in the bank, and it would go into effect immediately. Chairman Buie thanked Director Wright for the update, and said that when the senior building is complete, Wright can be left in charge of getting Bruno Mars to perform. She stated she would love that, but it would take about three ($3) million. Chairman Buie thanked everyone, and mentioned that the time for the next meeting is August 10th, at the Centre at University Park. Director Couch stated that Parks wanted to have more public input, so they are having more PopUps and Open Houses, and they have started to get that together starting in August. He stated that he would send out more information and invited them to join. With no further discussion Chairman Buie adjourned the meeting at 12:51 p.m. The meeting was adjourned.

Resources are continuing to update our job descriptions, monitoring certification requirements for our staff, which is important to knowing who is required to have licenses, CDL certifications, CPR certifications, etc. The purpose of this is to see who is in good standing, and is working to achieve that goal within a given timeframe. Parks has reintroduced LRSTATs, now called PARKSTATs, to measure how we are doing in different divisions within the department as a whole. All of the areas come together and give a presentation, taking a look at how we are progressing. We had our first meeting, and will have another meeting in September at the Centre on September 16th. The department is also in the process of allowing people to have flexible work schedules, being implemented through our HR department. This will allow staff to possibly come in earlier or work later, or even have a day off. However, everyone will still be required to work a full forty (40) hour work week. Rebsamen Golf has a Paul and Mary Lewis Tournament on September 16th, and this is an annual tournament that is about twenty-five (25) years old. This event is a two (2)-person scramble. This concludes Recreation, and asked for any questions to be directed to her. Chairman Buie then stated that he failed to ask if anyone had any question for Deputy Director Nelson, or Deputy Director Robinson. Operations Director Couch stated that he was still filling in for operations until they filled the position for Deputy Director. A big update was that MacArthur's Inclusive Playground is nearing completion, and they are looking at doing some kind of ribbon cutting around September. Kanis basketball has taken off and construction has started. Interstate roadway will be coming out for bid later in the month. This entails redoing all of the roadways in Interstate Park, which was needed a couple of years ago. Southside Park is getting new lights, and Couch mentioned he was thankful to the board and to ARPA for assisting with this. Our staff is currently building an Outdoor Learning Garden Center at West Central, and it was an in-house project. Also at West Central, design staff is looking at renovating the current ballpark, while looking at the total costs of the project. Martinez yield the rest of her time to Commissioner L. Smith Chairman Buie asked Commission L. Smith if there was any update. He stated that he loved working for the City, and serving the community with the game of golf. Bowden then thanked everyone for inviting him to speak. A couple of things he wanted to mention is that he was new, and things were different. He stated that First Tee was a junior facility, and was built in 2001 by the Jack Stephens Youth Golf Academy. The staff of First Tee do a great jobs, and he mentions that Director Blake does a great job with her staff and PGA Pro, and Brad Martin, the Director of Events, does a wonderful job as well. He is looking forward to working hand-in-hand with the staff from this point out, and bringing the community in, and showing them more with golf. Bowden mentions that one of his goals, being a Facility Supervisor, is to do different events. He mentions golf leagues, and doing clinics on the driving range. Bowden mentions that everyone knows that kids like other sports, yet the parents are not really involved with their competition. Golf is a little bit different, and gets the parent more involved, and this is something that he wants to bring to First Tee. He hopes that children can teach others, and move up to competitive golf. Peck stated that it turned out the way they wanted it to, and that Parks staff would be hammered with questions about how the money would be spent. Wright congratulated Couch, and told him that he has some money to play with. She stated that she told him that she would help, and she did. She stated that like Director Peck stated that the turnout was low, but it went the way we wanted. They are as follows: Champion of the Year, Titled Serving from the Heart, and was awarded to Robert Williams, and is centered on volunteerism. The third award was Festival of the Year, which was awarded for 11+ years to Little Rock Marathon. The fourth award was Indoor Facility of the Year ($1 million-$5 million), which was awarded to the West Central Community Center. The fifth award was Natural State Trail of the Year, which was River Mountain. Nelson thanked everyone who found time to pitch in and help write summaries for those awards. Executive staff will be traveling to the annual National Recreation and Parks Association Conference, which will be held in Phoenix, Arizona. They will be leaving in the coming week. Nelson stated that it would be a great time to learn, network, and get more ideas for our department. With that, Deputy Director Nelson closed her statements, and was thanked by Chairman Buie and Director Couch. Recreation Deputy Director Shawanda Robinson started reports by mentioning that she asked Deputy Director Nelson to send everyone a copy of the report, and there were some laying on the table. Rebsamen Tennis was the first topic. The center has and ATA 55 and older sectional tournament the upcoming weekend, 16th and 17th, and encouraged everyone to go and check things out. West Central Community Center will have an Open House later on in the evening, and will have light refreshments. She invited the Commission to come out from 6:00 p.m. - 7:30 p.m. There will also be a boxing event on September 28th through October 1st. The West Central Health Clinic will have a grand opening on September 29th, at 3:00 p.m. Robinson stated she would send out an email with more information about this, and encouraged participation from the Commission. The pool at Southwest Community Center has closed, and there will be an Open House at this facility on September 15, 2022 from 6:00 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. Rebsamen Golf Course will have the Paul and Mary Lewis Golf Tournament on Friday, September 16th. This is an annual tournament that has been around for about 25 years, and it is a two-person scramble (men, women, and seniors). Robinson encouraged and invited everyone out to the tournament, whether they were a golfer, or just wanted to see the event. First Tee will have its Open House on September 28. They will showcase their facility and will have games and refreshments. Therapeutic Recreation Division will do an East End "I Can" Arts and Resource Volunteer Clean-Up on September 22nd. Therapeutic will also start their volunteer services, in conjunction with the Little Rock Zoo monthly on September 27th. The Adult Annual Camping Trip will be held on September 28th through 30th at Camp Aldersgate. They will also do a Weekend Warriors program starting on September 23rd. MacArthur Museum will have a songwriting retreat for veterans and their families, hosted by The Freedom Sign USA. A two-day music workshop presentation, and live performance on August 25th and 26th. Robinson invited everyone to come out and join the facility. Their Open House will also be on September 26th. This concludes Recreation. Director Couch and Chairman Buie thanked Robinson for her report. Operations Director Couch stated that he was still filling in for Operations until the position is filled for Deputy Director. Current projects are continuing, and he will share exciting news. For the money that has recently been passed for improvements for Little Rock Parks and Recreation department, starting off the vote for the bond was successful. With this, Parks will receive over $24 million in bond improvement money. Parks is currently going out to the public and having public meetings, and Couch invited all to participate and shared that he would give out the information to those who wanted it. The meetings are for input on those funds. The Board also passed last week, utilizing some American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds, money totaling $2 million for community center improvements. Couch invited the Commission to give input on ideas for community centers. Also, there was another $3 million for seniors. This money goes towards a senior center, which is not located, nor are there any plans, but Couch hoped that one of the City Directors would be present to carry on the conversation. There is another $1 million for the West Central Ballfield Complex. Parks is currently working on visualizing what those improvements would look like. This is the first time since the sales tax over ten (10) years ago, that this much money has gone into Parks for improvements. Couch then welcomed Director Wright, and thanked her for assisting with getting money for Parks. This concludes Operations. Director Couch and Chairman Buie gave the floor to questions but none were asked at the time. Parks Maintenance Parks Maintenance Manager, J.P. Rogers opened parks maintenance reports by stating that they were mowing grass and praying for the first frost. Mr. Rogers told the Commission that everything is moving along and he hopes to see some improvements; Crews and contractors are moving along good, and he is in the process of getting budget requests together. This concludes Maintenance. Rogers gave the floor for questions but none were asked at the time. With no further reports, Chairman Buie proceeded to move down the agenda to old business. Old Business Chairman Buie opened up old business by mentioning the subjects of the last meeting, stating that he did not feel the need for a discussion on those topics. Then proceeds to New Business. New Business Chairman Buie opens discussion with stating that he wanted to acknowledge a new commission member, Mr. J.T. Ferstl. The Commission met Mr. Ferstl at the previous meeting, which he attended virtually. Due to technical issues, he could not tell about himself. Mr. Ferstl started off by stating that he had a real estate valuation and consulting business in Little Rock. He was born and raised in Little Rock, and was a graduate of Catholic High. He went to school in Fayetteville, and law school here in Little Rock. He has had numerous opportunity to serve the community and the city, and looks forward to continuing that with the Parks. In terms of his passion for him, Ferstl stated that he believes in youth sports. He thinks that it is a big thing that is missing in terms of facilities, and there has been a lot of studies done on children that play organized sports read more, their brains function on a higher level, and their less likely to get into trouble. For him, it is his driving force and anything that he can do on that front is what he plans on doing. Chairman Buie thanked him, and Director Wright stated she had a question. She asked his name, and said that she wants to work with him. She mentioned that youth sports is her heartbeat, sports for youth and keeping kids out of trouble. The next topic is sub-committee reports. Two committee chairs were absent, both for Master Plan and Social Media. Chairman Buie asked if there were anything given to Director Couch about this, and there were none. Chairman Buie mention that for the record, the Commission has three standing sub-committees, with two being listed on the agenda, and one needing to be added. They are Master Plan, Social Media and Outreach, and Parks Conservancy Liaison. With two sub-committee chairs being absent, he turned to the Parks Conservancy Liaison committee, Commissioner Ren Bressinck. Commission Bressinck started off by thanking Chairman Buie. Bressinck stated that he knows that from the Social Media and Outreach front, there was a lot of energy put into coming up with a membership drive plan. He felt as if this was something that was certainly needed. The intent would be that it would be something that fell under the Parks Conservancy, and no much under the Commission. They are continuing to build on it. In the past, prior to Bressinck getting on the Commission, the Conservancy was doing those activities. They had a Facebook page, and other aspects. He hopes to restart this and get back together with the other sub-committees. There will be more updates as things progress. This concludes the Committee Reports. Next topic is the presentation of our Parks guest, and Buie turned the floor over to Couch. Parks Guest Director Couch stated that our special presentations are another staff presentation to inform the Commission on what we do in Little Rock Parks and what great employees and staff we have. With this, he welcomed Jordan Mays, who is the Trails Coordinator. He has all of the trails in the department to maintain and look after. He was particularly hired to maintain our River Mountain Trail system and mountain biking trail. At this, he invited Mays to speak Mr. Mays thanked the Commission for being present, and stated he has the pleasure of serving as the trails coordinator for the Parks and Recreation department. He states that he will talk about some trails projects and current inventory. For projects, Mays that he has been with the city for seven month and for the first season, they were gaging the maintenance needs of the trail system. He hopes to create an appropriate action plan to manage the trails better. The second project is River Mountain Park. They are currently constructing a trail hub or landing pad at the bottom of Gravity Trails for mountain biking. This new improvement will be much safer and user-friendly for both users and pedestrians, and he is excited about that. The next project is coming up after the first of the year, and it is Boyle Park Multiuse Mountain Trails. With this, he is excited to announce he is working with a local contractor to build the trails. The last project is the Data Collection phase. This is an ongoing project which will help to develop a maintenance plan for maintaining trails. Updated maps will be provided to the public via the website platform. Pinpointing areas for maintenance, so information can be relayed both quickly and efficiently. Finally, he mentioned the Trail Inventory for the department. Mays said that it is good to have something on paper. This leads to inventory. All of these efforts GIS measured, and he tries to insure accuracy. Parks has been busy compiling that information on all of the trails, and so far, there is spatial data on twenty-four (24) parks, with 16.29 miles of paved trails, 15.16 miles of natural surfaced trails, and 9.86 of paved trails that is not within the park system. Next is a 4.5 mile water trail that extend from Benny Craig to Interstate Park that was obtained on the GIS system. Last, they also collected 8.45 miles of mountain biking and multiuse trail information on River Mountain trail, which is one of his favorite and was the recipient of the ARPA Natural Surface Trail of the Year. In its totality, we have 54.26 miles collectively, and there is still more work to do. Mays stated that he is happy to say that this project is almost complete. Riverfront, MacArthur, Western Hills and Hindman are still left to be completed. He is hopeful to be finished by the end of the fall season. This concludes Mays' presentation, and he thanked the Commission for the opportunity to work. He opened the floor to questions, but none were asked. Chairman Buie asked for any questions or comments, to which Director Couch raised his hand. He thanks Mays for the work he has done and stated that he had another special guest: Michael Garrity from Marathon. Couch stated that Garrity had a quick press announcement on the previous day and stated that he would love for Garrity to give a few updates on the Little Rock Marathon. Mr. Garrity thanked the Commission and stated that they were in their twenty-first (21st) year. They always take place in the first weekend in March, so March 4th and 5th this year is race weekend. Generally, they except between ten and fifteen thousand (10,000-15,000) participants and a total more than twenty to twenty-five thousand (20,000-25,000) people with their families and friends. Garrity stated that the Marathon brings in people from all fifty (50) states, and fourteen (14) different countries. The race is known for its medal, which was revealed the previous day. Garrity stated that the medals were all over social media and the television. He stated that registration is open, and there is a free training program that is year-round and invited the Commission to attend. With the program, there are two volunteers who have been with Marathon since day one, and they plan out a training plan for whatever distance you want to run. He told how to sign up and stated that it was free. Every year they have a kids' race. The children run their first twenty-five (25) miles during the school year, and it is generally a school-based program, or any group that gets the kids out and running. During race weekend, they run their final mile, and get the chance to run and cross the big finish line like every other race. Garrity states that is it a great program that is all over the state. This year, he expects eighteen hundred (1,800) kids, kind of getting back to pre-Covid numbers on the kids race. Participation is not back up to pre-Covid numbers with the other races. They are not trying to be too aggressive, due to ordering medals and supply chain issues. Garrity stated that medals must be designed and ordered by May, so they were already out to order to get them by race day. The number of medals determines the number of participants allowed in the race. That is how they look at setting capacity for the race. There are several other races and events throughout the year. On October 22nd, they are having a Creep N' Crawl, a half marathon and 5K that happens at Two Rivers Park. It is all along Mr. Mays' trail system. On December 17th, there will be an Ugly Sweater Race. During the Ugly Sweater Race, you are encouraged to wear an ugly sweater, while during the Creep N' Crawl, you are encouraged to wear your Halloween costume. Marathon has a robust social media presence. They make many crazy videos and things, which is their niche. Garrity called Marathon the fun and games part of the Parks department, along with everything that Deputy Director Robinsons' department does. He stated that he truly couldn't do it without the rest of the department, during race week. The race is truly a department-wide event, with recreation, administration, and maintenance all pitching in to help. This concludes Garrity's presentation. Director Couch and Chairman Buie thanked Garrity for his presentation and opened the floor to questions. Commissioner Eldridge raised her hand. Eldridge stated she had a question and asked if the marathon route is going to be the same. Garrity stated that it would be. Changing the course for the marathon is a long and exhaustive process, and it requires a lot. If it does not require changing, it will not change. The course was changed in 2020, due to I-30 construction. Now, there is no plan to change it until after all the construction is done, because runners used to run over and under I-30 several times during the weekend of racing. When the construction process started, there was one big change, and there is no race going east of I-30 at this point. Once all that construction is complete, there is the possibility of moving the course back east to by the Airport. Chairman Buie asked for questions, and none were asked. Buie thanked both speakers for their information. Next up was discussion items for next meeting. Discussion Items for Next Meeting Next up was discussion items for next meeting. Chairman Buie stated that under the line for subcommittee reports, adding a line for the Parks Conservancy, making sure that Commissioner Bressinck ample time to speak. Buie asked for any additional comments for the next meeting. He stated that he wanted to add something for the social, as a reminder to talk about. It will be held on Friday, October 21st at Hill's Station, and Buie told all to put it on their calendars. Director Couch stated he would like to put a couple of point on the agenda. First, he would like to have an ongoing status update on projects, for the ARPA funding and the bond funding. This is to get both an update on where the staff is on these projects and director, and to gather input from the Commission. Chairman Buie thanked Director Couch for his points. Next up on the agenda is Board Liaison Feedback, with Director Doris Wright. Board Liaison Feedback Director Wright stated she had a lot to discuss. She stated that due to personal obligations, she missed the first part of the meeting. Wright invited the Commission out to the ribbon cutting on the 29th, which is a Thursday, at 2:30 p.m. at the West Central Community Center, for the health clinic. The Healthy Connections Community Health Network wants to turn into a fall fest, so Wright asked Deputy Director Robinson to get some vendors for the event. She also asked Director Couch to get an ice cream truck, which he stated that it was something they would discuss. Wright stated she is trying to get the mobile arcade truck, but not if it had guns on it, due to an increase in gun violence in the city. Robinson stated something about bouncy houses, and Wright mentioned that she would give her the event planners information to correlate a plan together. She stated that some may not have ever been to the Community Center, and that now it is an award-winning community center, and stated that she did not know if Director Couch mentioned it. Couch mentioned that it was already said. Wright stated that they needed to see the ball fields, because she allocated $1 million for that, and she feels as if they can leverage that to get the business community involved. September 30th, there will be a reception for a boxing club coming from Ireland. They will be boxing at the West Central Community Center gym on that Saturday at 7:00 p.m. Trio's will be hosting a reception on that Friday at 7:00 p.m. and invited everyone to come out. They are staying in Memphis, but due to cancellations, they will be boxing Little Rock. This has been in the works for about six (6) months. We have the state Golden Gloves for March 2023. She excitedly asked for everyone to come out. Wright wants to let everyone know that the Comic-Con for Literacy had an outstanding event. It was the first Comic-Con in a Community Center in Little Rock. It had a fantastic turnout, with actors dressed up as superheroes, such a Thor, Spiderman, Alvin and the Chipmunks, the woman from Suicide Squad. The children came dressed in costumes and won awards for best costume. Central Arkansas Library System (CALS) was a sponsor and brought three hundred (300) books in to give to the children. By the end of the event, all the books were gone. There was a panel discussion with a local comic book author and graphic artist, and the gentleman that coordinates the Comic Con at the Statehouse. The purpose is to make it an annual event, to encourage reading. Due to the success of the event, CALS stated that they would be stocking the Little Free Library, and Parks would not have too anymore. Also, the Memphis Grizzlies in on the 27th, doing a clinic for basketball. The Arkansas Travelers did it for the baseball. She mentioned to Mr. Ferstl that she wanted to work with him, partnership with both Arkansas Travelers and Memphis Grizzlies with 21st Century children. The details are being worked out. Commissioner Ferstl mentioned that if he could meet Ja Morant, he was all in. Wright stated that the Grizzlies were trying to expand their brand into Arkansas, and they enjoyed the environment of the facility. When walking into the center, the first picture that you see is a Memphis Grizzly. Wright stated that she does a lot of things that she doesn't fully understand, but knows it needs to get done. They want to turn it into an outreach program, being something like an ambassador program, to get the kids off the streets and into the center. She stated that she did not understand the game but did not mind watching it because kids love it. She stated that it could turn into a pilot program to be assessed at the end of the season and do the same thing with baseball. Ferstl stated that he thinks that it would be an awesome idea, and he has said for years that there is a NBA team across the bridge, and it is not hardly utilized. Wright stated that Director Couch said he was on board, and Couch is on board. He was waiting on the final scope of the project. Wright stated she wanted to tie it into a Simmons Bank Foundation grant. She stated that they wanted to do a CRA project with a financial literacy project. She stated that she told them that a financial literacy project would need to have an incentive to have parents start. She stated she wanted to have it start with the 21st Century program, due to being in its fifth (5th) year and anticipating another five (5) year funding. This would be tied with the family engagement piece that is required by the state grant. The parents have to get involved, in order to qualify for the grant. The other component is a CRA (Community Reinvestment Act) aspect. All financial institutions have to be in compliance with that, and in Ward 6, there are fourteen (14) lots that there are going to be single-family homes on, and the Housing department is closing on another sixteen (16) lots. In its totality, there will be thirty-one (31) lots available, and she requested five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) in CRA effort, to be able to help buy down the loan for the buyer. There is also a down payment and closing cost assistance through the city, making that home one hundred fifty thousand dollars ($150,000) or less, and financed by Simmons. In totality, thirty-one homes, with down payment and closing costs assistance and financed by Simmons. Also, Wright asked for a rehab program for owner occupied housing where the homeowner could qualify for replacement of plumbing or roofing regardless of credit. If sixty-two (62) years or older, they could qualify for additional funds for more extensive work from the City's Homeowner Rehab program. That goes back to Director Couch's wanting the homes to connect to the trail system and the community center. Malloy Street is where the sixteen (16) lots sit, and 46th would be a direct path to the center, right down the street from Kiwanis. She stated that you would notice a crossing light in front of the community center. The others are near Zion Street, Walker Street, and Union Park. It would be connected to the community center so that the poor kids Wright wants to reach will have access. Rock Region Metro has a transit system called Metro Connect, which is an affordable method to get around in Ward 6. The purpose is to put together a package that is specifically for West Central for the sports programs, so parents know that there is transportation, programming, education, and recreation, fitness center and radio, with all aspects. There is also a health clinic with behavioral health specialist. The approach is a holistic approach, everything being centered around the West Central Community Center. Wright stated that her firm belief is that a Community Center needs to serve the community where it is located, it needs to be an assessment of what's going on within the community and provides the outreach to that community in a place where they all feel comfortable coming to. With, she stated that she wants engagement from the Commission, since Ferstl stated he was in youth sports, and she had a great communication with the business community, and they have stated that they will support a fundraiser for the ballfields. One of the fields would be named after Dixon Flake and getting his family involved. With this, she stated that was her report and acknowledged that Director Peck could not come due to personal obligations. Chairman Buie thanked her for her report. The next meeting will be Wednesday October 12, 2022, at The Centre at University Park at 12:00 p.m. Meeting Adjourned.
