Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting Minutes March 8, 2023 - Minutes The Centre at University Park Attendance: Matt Buie, Lauren Eldridge (Virtual), Dustin Smith, J.T. Ferstl, Ben France, Samuel Ellis, Cannon Fletcher Absent: Linda Smith, Director Andrea Lewis, Director Capi Peck City Board of Director Liaison: Director Andrea Lewis, Director Capi Peck LRPR Staff: City Attorney Beth Carpenter, Leland Couch, Angela Nelson, Shawanda Robinson, J.P. Rogers, Briana Hatfield Welcome and Introductions: Chairman Buie called the meeting to order and welcomed everyone present. Chairman Buie proceeded with the agenda to the roll call and approval of February's minutes. Roll Call and Approval of Minutes: Briana Hatfield called the roll and Chairman Buie reported a quorum was six (6) members - in attendance. Chairman Buie thanked everyone for coming, and stated for everyone who is virtual to mute themselves, but leave their cameras on in order to be counted as present for the meeting. Chairman Buie then informed the members that both the February minutes, along with the March 8th minutes, would be approved at the April 12th commission meeting. Citizen Communication: Chairman Buie stated that there was no citizen communication today. Chairman Buie then called for any staff reports. Staff Reports: Director Leland Couch asked Deputy Director Nelson to begin staff reports with Resource Administration. Administration Deputy Director of Administration, Angela Nelson, reported that Employee Appreciation Week would be held May 8th through the 13th. Additionally, the employee of the year award selection process has begun, and the Parks and Recreation Dept. hopes to have a nominee before March 20. Resource Administration continues to monitor spending, which is currently at 4% compared to January. We had Revenue Compliance Training so that everyone is performing correctly. We had a Device Inventory meeting (mainly computers, laptops, and phones) with IT, where we developed a link so the administration could be more efficient with monitoring Park equipment. We had a department Inventory Asset meeting and will have training this week to monitor the overall assets, from office equipment to maintaining equipment and property, to be more accurate and efficient in accounting for what we have. We are moving forward with maintenance and administrative positions that need to be filled. We are also moving forward with accreditation standards and sections. We are in the process of deciding our administrative team sections and what we can be working on. Summer requisitions are completed, and we have over 100 positions: lifeguards, maintenance workers, cashiers, operators, and various other jobs. Please pass the word to anyone seeking parttime work. This concludes Resource Administration. Chairman Buie and Deputy Director Nelson gave the floor to questions. Commissioner asked if the Inventory Asset Training that Resource Administration is conducting is new or annual. Deputy Director Nelson said it occurs yearly and usually undertaken around mid-October, but we wanted to get a head start. Recreation Recreation Programs Coordinator Sedric Mayfield is standing in for Deputy Director Shawanda Robinson. He started reports by giving a brief overview of programming for community centers. Current programs include "Latch Key" program, which is an afterschool program--finishing up basketball for youth. Spring and summer programming opportunities include Junior Hoops, a basketball program for junior high and senior high school students. We will also be moving into soccer. In the summer, we will do our swimming, baseball, softball, and t-ball programs. Other activities we do outside of programming are the Father-Daughter dance, a Mother-Son dance, and Mardi-Gras. The seniors held a Mardi-Gras program at Southwest Community Center. Recreation has picked up much traction from social media. Departmental training includes Active Shooter training held by Little Rock Police Department and fire extinguisher training held by Little Rock Fire Department. MacArthur Museum hosts movies and maintains about 40 participants for each film. For athletics, the ball fields are starting to see more use with kickball, baseball, and softball programs starting up. This concludes Recreation. Chairman Buie and Recreation Programs Coordinator Mayfield gave the floor to questions. Commissioner Buie raised a question about getting the road into Interstate Park fixed. Director Couch answered that the mayor gave LRPR funding to improve the main road from the front entrance to the back entrance and remove some of the old infrastructure in the area that must be cleaned out. Parks opened a bid and chose Redstone as the contractor and are now waiting on the City Attorney's office to complete the contract. City Attorney Beth Carpenter will check with the lawyer in charge of that contract. Chairman Matt Buie asked Recreation Programs Coordinator Sedric Mayfield if he had the numbers for the participants in the kickball program. Mayfield stated that he could get that information for Chairman Buie. Director Couch added that for Interstate Park, there are several other things that the staff is looking to improve. They are working with vendors to get proposals for bleachers, picnic tables, and other amenities. Chairman Matt Buie handed the floor over to Operations Deputy Director Justin Dorsey. Operations Deputy Director Dorsey started his reports by highlighting a few of the big stories they have dealt with. The operation was a significant contributor to setting up the Marathon that took place this past weekend in downtown Little Rock. Dorsey mentioned the weather and wanted to explain Western Hills and the banana sculpture. He noted that everything was almost finalized except for the dirt work. He said that completing this project component was taking a little longer than usual due to the unpredictability of the weather (having a few sunny days interspersed with heavy rains). They have also started working on the lights at MacArthur, fencing in the Dunbar Gardens sign, and prepping to place the sculpture. Operations are also dealing with many graffiti issues in some parks and trying to stay on top of graffiti removal. Additionally, three full-time positions for trail crew have been posted and advertised. Chairman Buie and Deputy Director Dorsey opened the floor to questions. Director Couch commented that Dunbar Gardens is a community garden and was selected as a sculpture site. Weather permitting, the sculpture is supposed to be delivered on Friday and installed in the next few weeks. Director Couch invited the entire commission to come to celebrate its installation. Chairman Buie asked if the funds to combat graffiti come from the Parks and Recreation budget. Director Couch mentioned that they are responsible for the funds if it involves Parks and Recreation. He said that it could be handled either in-house or through the use of contractors. This week, the Mayor assigned a small group of staff to figure out different solutions to handle graffiti and trash cleanup for the City of Little Rock. Currently, the best way to report graffiti is to notify 311; then, the appropriate department can handle it. Commissioner Fletcher asked what the process was for graffiti removal. Director Couch stated that it depends. He referenced park bathrooms with so much graffiti and vandalism that LRPR hired a contractor or staff to repaint the entire facility. In some cases, changing the color or the tone of the paint discourages graffiti. In other locations, they power wash or soft wash it off. Commissioner France asked about bid documents with Allsop Park bike trails. He wanted to know if that was a simple improvement of the tracks or if it extended them also. Deputy Director Dorsey said they are now doing walkthroughs and looking at the Park. Director Couch added that the LRPR receives Recreational Program grants from the federal government, managed through the state highway department. LRPR applied for a Boyle Park contract and is waiting for the City Attorney's office to finalize that contract. LRPR is in the process of applying for the contract for Allsop Park. Deputy Director Dorsey is working on finalizing construction documents. Director Couch acknowledges that government contracts take some time to go through. Additionally, he clarified that the scope is not to change much in Allsop; instead, make it loop more and be friendly for mountain bikes and other users. Chairman Buie gave the floor over to Marathon and Emergency Management Assistant Mike Garrity Marathon Update They hosted the 2023 Little Rock Marathon, the 21st annual event. Everything went well. Both Saturday's 5k and 10k races were sold out. Sunday was the half-marathon and the Marathon, and LRPR was 98% sold out. They were working the way back to pre-covid numbers. I did not meet that, but I got closer. They had 1000 kids and 400 parents running, including Director Couch. They had a Health and Fitness Expo on Friday, which was a rousing success. The Recreation Department was part of that. Marathon engaged the rest of the Parks department this year; they were essential. The recreation side set up both days of the Expo and was there during the Athlete's Village, and everyone had a great time and was engaging; and trying to make that part of the experience more interactive. That portion was exciting and was the first time it had been done. It got a little warm Sunday during the Marathon, so the department had to implement safety protocols. Director Couch got a phone call regarding the issue, and all the public safety officials could execute the plan and were in place for further action if necessary. Thanks to both Little Rock and North Little Rock law enforcement and fire safety officials for their assistance. It was still conducting active cleanup, which should be complete by April. Chairman Buie called for questions for Mr. Garrity, and Commissioner France thanked Garrity and the department for the help and the resounding success. The media team got shots of volunteers and support and used these photos for a social media campaign. We had about 1000 volunteers. Director Couch thanked and specifically named Geneva Lamm, Mike Garrity, and Brandi Dixon, the three full-time Marathon staff. Chairman Buie asked about the route: is it the same each year, or does it change? It changed in 2021 due to the I-30 construction, but they try to keep it the same as much as possible. They get the Half-Marathon and the Marathon certified by US Track and Field so that Little Rock Marathon can qualify for the Boston Marathon. You must have a qualifier-certified course to compete in that specific Marathon. The certification is an undertaking to complete every year, so the department decided to change the system for 2021 so we stay within I-30 during their 5-year construction project. Once that project is completed, we will look at going back east because they want to have the race pass by the Clinton Library and the Airport area. Logistically the goal is to keep it the same after it has been set. Plan to change once more postconstruction. Commissioner Ellis mentioned that during the Expo, all he heard was compliments, and that precovid atmosphere was back. Saying the route of the Marathon, he wanted to know the best way to get updates on courses and detours for any barricades or crossings for pedestrian and bicycle traffic. Garrity answered that they currently post public signage up 30 days before events. They also post on social media but are taking suggestions for smoother and more efficient notice. Recreation Programs Coordinator Sedric Mayfield wanted to tip his hat to Recreation's Deputy Director, Shawanda Robinson for spearheading the Recreational division's engagement in the expo. She is on medical leave. Chairmen Buie closed questions and moved to Parks Maintenance Manager, J.P. Rogers. Parks Maintenance Parks Maintenance Manager J.P. Rogers opened park maintenance reports stating he did not do much. He did notify the commission that they are starting to cut grass. The biggest thing is if you have a 17�18-year-old teenager at home and you want them engaged in a summer activity, Parks Maintenance has a Parks Pioneer program that pays for summer positions. These positions are posted on the City of Little Rock's HR website. Parks Maintenance is looking to hire up to 19 students. Eight have applied so far. Chairman Buie asked for clarification--the program's name is Park's Pioneers. Director Couch elaborated that Park's Pioneers is a pre-covid program; this is the first year of it returning. Parks Manager, Rogers added that students work for 60 days (the summer), are trained, undergo interviews, are drug tested, and have limitations (no chainsaws). They work 40 hours a week, Monday through Friday. Chairman Buie called for questions. There were none. Director Couch added that this is the most challenging time of the year to keep up with the grass mowing. Cutting grass in the rain is complex, and the heat makes it unpredictable and possibly dangerous. This concludes Park Maintenance. Chairmen Buie once again mentioned Parks Pioneers and encouraged applications. With no further reports, Chairman Buie shifted the agenda to old business. Old Business Chairman Buie opened the old business with stating thanks to all commissioners as they had 100% attendance at the specially called meeting last month where the park property was transferred, and there was a unanimous agreeance to that. The commission heard from Ms. Hatfield about Boyle Park last month. Chairman Buie then proceeds to New Business. New Business Chairman Buie begins the next topic: sub-committee reports. First up is Social Media and Outreach, with Commissioner France is going to coordinate with Mike Garrity to discuss the social media state and go over the meaning they want to convey. Next up was the Master Plan Committee, with Commissioner Linda Smith, but she was absent, and Director Couch had nothing to discuss. Finally, the last sub-committee is Parks Conservancy, with Commissioner Lauren Eldridge, and the committee started the campaign for Parks Conservancy the previous month. Now, 5 of 7 commissioners have signed up as sustaining members of Friends of the Park. Encourages the other commissioners to join and share the group with friends and family. Chairman Buie asked if Commissioner Ferstl was going to add to that. Commissioner Ferstl mentioned that he signed up during the special meeting last month when it was first brought up and that it only took about 5 minutes and was super easy to do--he also encouraged the two remaining commissioners (Chairman Buie mentioned that he was signing up right then), to sign up as well as everyone watching. Chairman Buie then gave the floor to Director Couch for an update on projects. .Updates on Projects Chairman Buie moved on to the next agenda item from Director Couch, who would give updates on Kiwanis Park at the behest of Director Lewis. Director Couch mentioned in the Master Plan committee regarding updates. Kiwanis was highlighted for community input for improvements completed with the bond money. Little Rocks Parks and Recreation are working with different vendors for the basketball quotes (got one on March 08). Removed the playground with the intent to replace it, but lost money for the replacement and had been unable to complete it. It will be replaced as part of that bond package as well. Those are the improvements on the list currently. Director Couch is aware of the request from the community for splash pads and more parking. Those are still to be considered, but it depends on the amount of funding left over from the projects already allocated. It is located between Holt and Foster Street. Also working with the Kiwanis Club to help raise support. The schedules conflict, but they will be figured out and worked through. Director Couch opened the floor for questions on Kiwanis or other parks, and the Commissioner Fletcher asked about the parking lots and whether the barriers should be up or down. He mentioned that Kiwanis Park's community asked for a gate because it was requested to be closed at night and open in the mornings. It had been defuncted for some time, so now it's closed. Commissioner Fletcher mentioned that at Burns Park, the police lock the Park at night, and LRPR staff open parks in the morning. Director Couch said that opening or closing over 70 different parks location was not feasible in the long run. Chairman Buie asked if any of the commissioners had a park they wanted to be highlighted by LRPR staff. He mentioned that it didn't have to be now but just email Director Couch. Commissioner France was asking if Ward 1 had been done yet. Director Couch mentioned that most work was done in Ward 6 - Kiwanis and Boyle. He said that an East Little Rock report would be able to give much information as many things are being done. Commissioner France asked for Ward 1. Director Couch acquiesced. Golf tournament Chairman Buie returned the floor to Commissioner Eldridge to discuss the upcoming golf tournament. Commissioner Eldridge mentioned that there was not much to report on the golf tournament and that she did have flyers ready but wanted to make sure that the website for registration and sponsors was good to go before pushing those out. She mentions that she has a flyer for the sponsors ready to go. She estimated 1-2 weeks to check and verify the websites, and then she will start distributing them. She asked Commissioners if they could come up with a list of businesses or friends that own or are connected to local businesses to try and approach them with these sponsorship requests. All the information will be on the flyer; you can ask her for any additional information. I will talk to Mike Garrity about the registration portal and approach Matt for sponsorship payment options on the Park Conservancy front. The golf tournament will be on May 19, 2023. Chairman Buie asked for questions for Commissioner Eldridge. Commissioner France asked if she would reach out to them or if she wanted to split those duties up. She responded that she was unsure if she had sent that out yet, but she does have a list she needs to put on her computer and then send it out, and if anyone knows or would like to reach out to specific companies on the list, she would appreciate it. Commissioner Eldridge mentions that in the past, it's been hit-or-miss. There have been a few returning sponsors, but they often have to find new sponsors each year. Director Couch queried if Commissioner Eldridge had a flyer for the golf tournament that we could put on social media. [see the screen for a glimpse of the ad] Director Eldridge wants to verify whether the URL that is currently on the flyer is the one that corresponds to the registration portals before sending the flyer out. City Attorney Carpenter requested that there be a gatekeeper and that all verifications and comments be sent first to Director Couch from Commissioners to be in keeping with the Commission bylaws, and chairman Buie affirmed. Chairman Buie also mentioned adding Parks Conservancy to the golf tournament flyer. Commissioner Eldridge mentioned that she had planned to add it. Chairman Buie also noted a QR Code; Eldridge said she would work on that. Chairman Buie mentioned being on the lookout for an email from Director Couch regarding a social event. Buie thanked everyone for their reports and gave the floor to questions. None were asked. Discussion Items for Next Meeting This concludes the Committee Reports. The next topic is the agenda for the next meeting. Chairman Buie mentioned that an in-depth analysis of Ward 1 would be discussed at the next meeting. Director Couch requested to discuss the social media aspect of the Friends group. I want to discuss getting social media about it through Parks and Recreation. Chairman Buie mentioned that there would be a meeting with Mike Garrity presenting a joint social media account presenting the Friends group to the masses. Commissioner France asked to be included. The Parks and Recreation department is also hiring a Social Media & Marketing Coordinator. There was a similar position approximately four years ago, and it will be revamped from that, focusing on planning and implementing marketing strategies and ensuring that we have a consistent brand and integrity throughout the department. Regarding the payroll area, we have been challenged with coding or trying to capture all the work time related to tornado relief efforts, including volunteering. We started reports by giving a brief overview of programming for community centers. The department has wrapped up interviews for those two positions. The main feature is always a dance contest, and it's enjoyable. They also sell T-shirts so you can capture the moment of this 21st year. Therapeutic Recreation's Youth Summer Camp registration started on April 10th. It will be at the War Memorial Clubhouse from June 12th to July 21st. New Business Director Couch began by asking if anyone in the room was personally affected by the tornado. Director Couch then explained that Parks and Recreation had three majorly damaged parks: Rock Creek Park in West Little Rock�there's a trail system out there, and we had some significant infrastructure damage. We haven't been able to review it 100% because it's so extensive in terms of its location and the fact that it's hard to get to because of so many downed trees. The aerial slide accompanying the presentation is a before and after interactive map showing previous and after conditions due to the tornado. You can slide a bar across the screen that displays. Reservoir Park was also damaged by the Jackson Reservoir on Highway 10. The tornado went from end to end of the park and was completely destroyed. We lost essentially every asset in the park, a pavilion, the disc-golf course, a playground, and the tennis and ballfields were affected. The biggest thing that we lost was all the tree cover. We lost thousands of pine trees. We are currently working through how to salvage some of those trees and process all the damage in the park. Reservoir Park is being used as a dumping site for the city of Little Rock, so residents can go and dump their debris there. We are working with Public Works in terms of the whole operation. It is very substantial and includes house debris. We will grind and remove all of that. Reservoir Park will be completely renovated, but it will be a closed park for at least a year, if not two, due to the extent of the damage. You can see the ground on the left, which indicates the damage. The only standing area is between the ball field and the residents. Those are the only trees left. The other park that Director Couch mentioned was Murray Park. The tornado crossed Murray Park and damaged Rebsamen Park Road and everything on the south side of Rebsamen Park Road. It went straight through a swampy area, missing our pavilions, but it caused damage to our Fit Lot, our sand volleyball courts, significant tree damage, and then the dog park had extensive damage. Our Urban Forestry and Maintenance staff have done a great job clearing the debris, and there is soccer practice tonight. Code enforcement was able to help, and volunteers have been great at helping pick up. There are still issues at Murray, which will be for many months. We do not want to advertise it as being open, but certain areas will slowly be reopened to the citizens as we get them safe and transparent for public use. The next big area we are trying to open is the dog park, which staff has reported that hopefully, it should be open by this weekend. We did mention that FEMA is utilizing West Central, which will be ongoing, they don't know their exact time frame, but the Recreation staff moved everything out of there. That was a big lift, but we have been able to work with everyone on all the reservations and all the displacements, but Director Couch believes that it has all been worked out. Hopefully, we can provide a better schedule to the citizens of when that will be back available to the public, but we don't know that now. Director Couch then opened the floor up to questions after praising Marathon and Emergency Management Assistant, Mike Garrity for taking charge at the EOC, which is down on 7000 Murray Street, the Emergency Command Center. Director Couch then gave the floor to Mike Garrity to answer questions or add information. Chairman Buie opened the floor for questions. Director Couch thinks it will be finalized in the next week. Additionally, most people can and are detouring around that. Chairman Buie asked how is all the extra cost from the storm being covered by the Parks and Recreation Dept. That process is one Mr. Garrity could cover well, because if there were any detailed questions, he was the one to help with the big flood in 2019 and managed all of our reimbursements on a lot of that. Everything that we have seen so far is in a process. It's just trying to figure out whether it is a repair or a replacement and if it just takes time to do all that. So we haven't even started on any repairs yet; we have only been focused on cleanup efforts and assessing what is damaged. When we went to Murray Park, we couldn't get in for the first three or four days because of the high power voltage lines down, and we looked from afar and looked at the pavilions and found all eight pavilions were all good; it looked like the roofs were intact. Until J.P. walked around the backside and saw all the pavilions' backside roofs were damaged. I don't know how that happened because the tornado was going across the river, but the backwind effort destroyed them. So they will have to be rebuilt or the roofs replaced. There's always something new that we find every time we go out, so we do a lot of that. We do have staff putting up caution tape and signs. We ask citizens to stay off anything affected by the tornado because we don't know realistically the full extent of the damage until we review it. The museum continued its 2023 "Movies at MacArthur" film program in March with the documentary The Hello Girls. The film examined efforts by the U.S. Army Signal Corps in 1918 to send 223 women to France as telephone operators to help win World War I. By war's end, they had connected over 26 million calls and were recognized by General John J. Pershing for their service. The April "Movies at MacArthur" film, Unsettled History: America, China and the Doolittle Tokyo Raid, is scheduled for April 18, which is the 81st anniversary of the raid. In conjunction with the movie, the museum will debut a new exhibit on the raiders, From Shangri-La to Tokyo: the Story of the Doolittle Raiders. Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting Minutes May 24, 2023 The Centre at University Park Attendance: Matt Buie, J.T. Ferstl (Virtual), Ben France (Virtual), Samuel Ellis, Cannon Fletcher, Mike Bernardo Absent: Director Peck, Director Andrea Lewis, Lauren Eldridge, Linda Smith, Ron Bara City Board of Director Liaison: Director Andrea Lewis, Director Capi Peck LRPR Staff: Leland Couch, Angela Nelson, Shawanda Robinson, Justin Dorsey, Briana Hatfield, City Attorney Beth Carpenter Welcome, and Introductions: Chairman Buie called the meeting to order and welcomed everyone present. Chairman Buie then introduced the two new commissioners to the meeting: Ron Bara (not present) and Mike Bernardo. Chairman Buie asked Commissioner Bernardo to introduce himself and give a brief explanation as to why he got involved. Commissioner Bernardo mentioned that he was retired military, he served active and reservist, a retired IT Manager, has four children, and very familiar with the use of Parks and Recreation; He coaches competitive and recreational sports and plays golf and volleyball, etc., an active Pickle ball player. Also, play a lot at Kanis Park (familiar with that area). He has no particular reason in joining the Commission other than he thought he could contribute and hoping that he can because it is an important part of the community. Chairman Buie thanked him for his service and mentioned that he looked forward to working with him. He then proceeded to roll call and the approval of April's minutes. Roll Call and Approval of Minutes: Briana Hatfield called the roll, and Chairman Buie reported that a quorum in attendance was six (6) members. Chairman Buie thanked everyone for coming; Chairman Buie then asked for the April 24th minutes to be approved. The motion passed, and the minutes were approved. Citizen Communication: Chairman Buie yielded the floor to Ryan Pruitt of Walton Heights Homeowner's Association Board for Citizen Communication. Mr. Pruitt thanked Briana Hatfield for setting up his computer for his presentation. He came to request help designing and perhaps funding a neighborhood and community playground in their neighborhood, located at the trailhead of River Mountain Drive. Utilizing his computer, he provided a diagram of where the project would be, between Conner Park and Two Rivers Park. Their HOA was funded over 50 years ago with over 500 homes. The point of the project site is the trailhead of the River Mountain Trail with mountain bikes. It is a hub right now for their community, especially the mountain biking community. Their desire as a neighborhood would be to use Little Rock land to build a playground in conjunction with the Parks and Recreation Dept. They are petitioning to use Parks and Recreation property on the South or North side of South Ridge Drive. Mr. Pruitt has walked the site with Director Couch and Director Peck. Mr. Pruitt mentioned that the area slopes significantly, so there's a great opportunity to build a beautiful terrace and playground. Talking with Director Couch we looked at some ideas where we could have a cascading playground option with slides and swings and ropes, and all ADA accessible. They would have ramps connecting down the terrace with a view towards the south if we built on the South side of South Ridge, and or on the North it looks down toward the cascading mountain bike trail. That is our request, for you to approve the use of City property, either for Walton Heights to build it ourselves, or partnering with you to build it together with a matching possibility. Chairman Buie then asked for questions and comments for Mr. Pruitt. Commissioner Fletcher mentioned that he's walked the trail from Conner Park. He continued that it's a unique spot to have an intersection for the neighborhood. Director Couch commented that he appreciated Mr. Pruitt's presentation and mentioned that he liked the idea of partnering, because Parks and Recreation partners with a lot of people on different projects, so he would like to hear more about that in the future. Chairman Buie thanked Mr. Pruitt once again and Commissioner Ben France asked if it was City Park land that Mr. Pruitt was requesting the use of. Mr. Pruitt confirmed it was. Director Couch then clarified that the land is currently River Mountain Park which has a mountain bike trail facility in part of it, that goes across South Ridge. There is Park land there that is not dedicated to an actual park, is in between River Mountain and Conner Park. Conner Park is a bigger western park with 10 acres on Cantrell Road. Commissioner France asked if there was a power line easement nearby, and Director Couch confirmed it was. He also mentioned that it had somewhat been addressed as far as making sure if a playground was done there that it does meet powerline constraints. Those are some of the details that the neighborhood has been looking into to ensure there is no conflict. Commissioner Ellis mentioned that this was a great spot in the neighborhood. He lives near the area and has heard some of the ideas and thoughts going behind the playground. He commented that it would be a great way to connect the neighborhood to Conner Park and what Parks and Recreation is doing with mountain biking on the South side and the North side as well as having some type of park or playground equipment. Some questions proposed were: would that affect any of the parking? There are just a couple of spaces, so would that affect that? Or would it be behind there? Mr. Pruitt responded that one of the benefits they saw was that there was already on site parking. Most families would be able to walk there, but the idea is that it would be down the hill. With ADA they are looking at ramps and switchbacks, but also you would be able to have a bridge that would go straight out from the parking lot to an upper raised playground and terrace and then go down from there. Director Couch also commented that Commissioner Ellis' concerns were valid, and that a lot of the neighborhood parks don't have parking facilities, and the logic behind that is that it's their neighborhood park, and they shouldn't have to drive there, so that's one concept. However, before this grew legs any further, there would need to be a public meeting that the neighborhood would be invited to, and they could share their concerns. Another way to handle that is to make sure that the neighborhood and everyone that's involved in that adjacent area would be on board and understand the project. Commissioner Ellis clarified that it wasn't so much of a concern as it was wanting more information. He believes it's an interesting idea and would benefit many children in the neighborhood. It would be really great to have something like that so close to the neighborhood, that wouldn't require extra parking. He knows that the current parking is used by mountain bikers and hikers and wouldn't want to interfere with that. Chairman Buie then rounded out that portion of the commission meeting by mentioning and clarifying that additional public meetings would need to be held, as well as additional conversations with Parks and Recreation. If something comes from those meetings then it would be brought back before the commission. City Attorney Beth Carpenter mentioned that with City-owned property, if we are talking about the potential leasing of City property, according to the state statute, that would need to be bid out. Director Couch responded that there would be no leasing, to his understanding. If this project made it to ground it would actually be just a project for Little Rock Parks and Recreation to build an amenity for the neighborhood and the citizens of Little Rock. Chairman Buie then called for any staff reports. Staff Reports: Director Couch asked all staff to go down the list with their reports after introducing all the Deputy Directors to Commissioner Bernardo. He then handed the floor to Deputy Director Angela Nelson to begin staff reports with Resource Administration. Administration Deputy Director of Administration, Angela Nelson, informed the commission that there was a date change from May 10th to May 24th, expressed appreciation that the members could still come and apologized for any inconvenience that may have caused. As a department, Parks and Recreation wrapped up employee appreciation week. The department was given the opportunity to select employees of the year, and one of those candidates was Michael Garrity, the Marathon and Emergency Management Assistant. He has been with the city for 12 years. The other was Linda Bealer. She works at Stephens Community Center and is the Facility Supervisor. The department selected them because they were very deserving of that award and recognition. The department is still working on the Statement of Value Inventory. Because of the storm damage we are evaluating a lot of assets that we have, things that are missing and need to be accounted for. We are still working on that, and in conjunction to that we are working on our division capital assets, which involves all assets. We are just trying to stay on top of that so we can get a head start and be completed with this by the end of the year. Our Summer Playground Program starts June 12th, and we are still trying to reach our goals of getting people staffed in positions. We are really close to reaching those goals. As a department we have filled 8 positions. 5 were in maintenance, 1 in administration, and 2 in recreation. By the end of the month we will possibly have two more candidates for filling two more positions. We hope to get everything filled by September. That concludes my report on resources. Chairman Buie thanked Deputy Director Nelson for her report and then called for questions. There were none, so Chairman Buie gave Deputy Director Craig the floor. Recreation Recreation Programs Deputy Director Shawanda Craig greeted the floor by discussing the status of West Central and FEMA. FEMA will continue to be stationed at West Central until June 8th. She will give an update on that if it does extend longer than June 8th. The pools are open at Jim Dailey Fitness Center and Southwest pool will open on May 27th. The Summer Playground Program will begin on June 12th and go through July 27th. They are still taking registrations, and it is $100 per child. Jim Dailey pools will start swimming lessons soon so if you have anyone that would like to become a lifeguard, we are still seeking lifeguards. Please check in with the staff at Jim Dailey and Southwest. They will have to go through a prerequiste course and then the Red Cross training to become a lifeguard. Once they are certified then we can employ them as a lifeguard for the city of Little Rock. MacArthur has a traveling exhibit: Military Women's Memorial in Arlington. They will be here Saturday, June 17th, through August 26th. Therapeutic Recreation will have their summer camp at War Memorial golf course. We are making changes there, hopefully, once we get that completed we can invite you guys out to look at our new space. The golf tournament at Rebsamen was a success, and the staff enjoyed having you all there playing golf this past Saturday. Deputy Director Robinson concluded her report, and Chairman Buie called for questions. Commissioner Ben France asked in regards to the Summer program, how many kids on average are there. Deputy Director Craig responded that East Little Rock will have 100, Stephens will have 120, Dunbar will have 210, and we have two schools: Baseline Elementary� 150, and Washington Elementary will have 150. It's $100 for 7 weeks. There are additional activities and programs that these places provide but they also cost for the children to attend. With no more questions, Chairman Matt Buie handed the floor over to Operations Deputy Director Justin Dorsey. Operations Deputy Director Dorsey started his reports by mentioning Urban Forestry and the aftermath and cleanup of the tornado. Just this past month the Urban Forestry division has removed more than 100 damaged trees, not counting limbs. We are working on developing plans to plant more trees. There are a couple grant opportunities, we are in the research and partnering phase with a couple different garden clubs to possibly get some grants for new tree planting opportunities. Splash pads will be opening this Friday. The guys have all those painted, caulked, and pressure-washed clean so we are excited that all four of the splash pads will be open at 10 am. They will be open 10 am to 9 pm every day. With the Design and Operations division we have Dunbar Gardens. The new sculpture there, the dedication was this past month. We appreciate the commissioners that came out and were present. That meant a lot to staff to see you all come out and support. We are working on several new site plans, and new projects are coming: Boyle, Kiwanis, and Pankey Parks. We're getting ready to start on designs for that. As Deputy Director Craig mentioned, we are wrapping up renovations for War Memorial Pro Shop. When that space gets finished we would love to have you all out to see that new purpose space. We look forward to program and rent out that area. The guys completed several repairs at Southwest and Jim Dailey and the outdoor pool facilities. In addition to that, the guys have done a really good job of being able to manage these projects. There's a new service entrance gate at Boyle, and it was done completely in-house. We were having a lot of illegal dumping at Boyle, and they were able to get it taken care of in between other projects. Chairman Buie and Deputy Director Dorsey opened the floor to questions. Commissioner Fletcher asked if War Memorial Pro Shop was going to be a staff location or event space. Deputy Director Dorsey responded that it would be a rentable event space. With no further questions, and no other staff reports, Chairman Buie shifted the agenda to old business. Old Business Chairman Buie opened the old business by asking if there were any updates or new information regarding the tornado damage. Director Couch mentioned that they are still moving forward with cleanup and that their contractor DRS has been working diligently at Reservoir and have cleared most of the down trees, and Murray's cleanup is coming along too. Rock Creek is the next big focus out there. Director Couch mentioned that he had covered it a lot during this meeting, but also stated he was open to questions. Chairman Buie mentioned that he saw some bins outside of Butler Park, and inquired as to what they were for. Director Couch stated that Public Works put some waste containers to put people can put debris and trash into. He was unsure about how long they were going to be there. Chairman Buie looked over old business concerning Park highlights, the golf tournament, and the social event. He asked if there were any questions about the old business as of yet. Commissioner Fletcher brought up the free Little Rock Open, and invited everyone to come out and spectate. He mentioned that last year's winner won the Australian Open's doubles tournament, and the guy he beat Ben Shelton, is now 35 or 37 in the world. Several of the competitors are also in the top 100. He reiterated that the Open was free this year and that there were new sponsors, so it would be great to have good attendance. He mentioned that there is a sign in the front, but it states that there has been about $6 million worth of community impact from all the events and tournaments. He just wanted to highlight that. Deputy Director Craig thanked the commissioner for bringing it up because it was something that both she and Director Couch wanted to touch on. Director Couch mentioned that it was from May 28th through June 4th. He mentioned that it was a bigger event for the department. He mentioned Parks and Recreation now has a three-year commitment with UAMS. Director Couch, then requested the commission move on to New Business and Chairman Buie then turned the floor over to Director Couch. New Business Director Couch began by mentioning that he has gotten all their bond and ARPA projects approved. One of the bond projects was getting new lights at Rebsamen Tennis Center. Out of ARPA funds, the senior center is one of the projects being handled. They had a kickoff meeting to approve vendors and professional services for design of the community centers and senior center. The senior center is in the Centre at University Park. An aspect of that design is the Pickleball complex, and that will come online in the near future. It will tie this facility into the Rebsamen Tennis Center. Director Couch also briefly wanted to cover the other bond and ARPA projects. The professional design services are expected to be finished with their part of the project before the end of the year, so that they can put it out to bid early next year to have some improvements to the community centers. They will focus on four of the community centers, the senior center, and the West Central ball field complex for the ARPA projects. Commissioner France asked for more information regarding the senior center. Director Couch explained that currently The Park at University is closed for board and commission meetings, but the idea is that they will be able to repurpose this facility slightly. Realistically add on to the southern end of this building, and concepts are looking at more space and a therapeutic pool, and the different aspects of what that would be. For many years there has been the thought to add a Pickleball facility to Rebsamen Tennis, and so when the discussion to move seniors to the facility started, Parks and Recreation thought it would be a good idea to house those projects together. There are no drawings at this time, and are open to receiving input. Score Card Analysis Director Couch wanted to start a process for more city-wide engagement. He suggested to do a quick study with the Commissioners. Using some small note cards, he asked the Commission to write about what they think the most important things are in facilities and programs that they have. Write two items under each of these four categories: Recreation, Programs, Facilities, and the last one is other, where you can put anything you want. Then at the next meeting, Director Couch will do this again, and in between this meeting and next, use that opportunity to research some more about Little Rock Parks and Recreation. We'll take this meeting's information and see who's familiar with what, and next month we'll have more defined. We'll combine that information and narrow it down to five top things that we really want to market and promote, pushing it to the top of everything we talk about. If you would like to email in topics that is appreciated also. Chairman Buie called for questions, and seeing there were none, moved on to the next topic. Future Dates in Webex Director Couch apologized for having to move the meeting date because of personal conflicts. In the future he will do his best not to have to move dates around again. He started looking down on the calendar to make sure there were no other conflicts, and unfortunately there is one in October, which coincides with a national conference. The majority of the people that attend the commission will be at that conference, so he wanted to know what the commission wanted to do about the meeting, whether they would prefer substitutes to present the information, or change the date entirely. The only Parks and Recreation staff member that would not be at the conference would be Mike Garrity. Director Couch was not expecting an immediate answer, but instead wanted to bring it to the commission's attention so that it could be resolved. Regarding Webex, Director Couch wanted it known that he preferred in-person meetings, but he knows that Webex is something that will always be there. He is willing to discuss continuing Webex but wanted to have that conversation at least. Chairman Buie asked the commission to give their thoughts on changing commission dates in the future and how to handle it. Director Couch mentioned that staff would be gone for about 4 days, so it would not be feasible to change the date for another one that same week. He also mentioned that some commissioners had reached out and informed him that they had put that meeting on their calendar and so any date changes would need to be well in advance. Chairman Buie asked the commission to be thinking about an alternative date that would work for the majority of the members, so that it can be discussed at the next meeting. Sub-committee Reports Chairman Buie then turned to the sub-committee reports. First up is Social Media and Outreach with Commissioner France. There was no report. Next up was the Master Plan Committee, with Commissioner Linda Smith. There was no report. Finally, the last sub-committee is Parks Conservancy. The liaison was not present, but Commissioner Fletcher asked Chairman Buie if he could give an update on a ballpark estimate of how many people have signed up. Chairman Buie mentioned that about 10 people have signed up so far. In the last Conservancy meeting they agreed that they will put together a formal plan announcing things and bringing everything to light. Look for more information on that in the future. They are hoping to have some media announcements, announcing that the conservancy is supporting some local projects with funds that have been raised by the Conservancy. They are looking also to have some events scheduled in the future as well so that people can come out and learn more about the Conservancy. The Conservancy's mission is to support Little Rock Parks and Recreation, its the nonprofit 501c3 partner so fundraising is the name of the game. Getting more people engaged hopefully will get more people in the friends program and lead to individual contributions. Chairman Buie ended the report on that, and before moving to discussion items for next meeting Director Couch wanted to mention a couple of dates. The Little Rock Open (May 28th- June 4th) and Mud Run at War Memorial on Markham on the 18th fairway on June 3rd. The last event, which is not a public event but is on June 5th, will be floating Fish Creek. It will be launching from Benny Craig Park at 10 am. This is something that we are doing to take different people down the creek to show them. We are also introducing it to our newer staff. It is one of the official water trails in the city. It is a beautiful area that is unfortunately full of trash but that's another story to address later. Commissioner France asked about canoes, and Director Couch responded that there might be some extra rooms in the existing facilities that they have. They are working with Norm Berner, who got all the canoes from Audoban, Arkansas and he is filling those up. Director Couch is bringing his own, as well as staff. Commissioner Ellis also volunteered to help anyone that might not have access to their own canoe. Director Couch expressed his appreciation for the commissioners that came out to the sculpture and asked that if they wanted to come to any of the other events please let him know. Discussion Items for Next Meeting This concludes the Committee Reports. The next topic is the agenda for the next meeting. Chairman Buie asked to add a section to next meeting's agenda for upcoming events so that we have it there every month. Chairman Buie then asked if there was anything else that needed to be added to the agenda, and Commissioner Bernardo mentioned that he had a couple questions. The first question was regarding security. He mentioned that he knows park security is a huge thing, especially out at Kanis, because it impacts the reputation and the draw. He mentioned that he would like to add that to the agenda and maybe discuss with the police for any information. Director Couch agreed and mentioned that he has reached out to LRPD a lot, but will see if they can send a representative to the next meeting to inform the commission about what's going on. He mentioned that LRPD is doing a lot of great things but to let them hear from us and what our concerns are would be better, as well as letting us understand what they are or are not doing. Chairman Buie asked that we put security as a new business item for next month's meeting. Commissioner Bernardo's next question concerned Pickleball. He mentioned that if anyone wanted him to give a 5-10 minute overview of what Pickleball is and how it's growing in the communities around us, he would be more than willing. Chairman Buie thanked him and mentioned that they have heard so much about Pickleball in the last 5-6 years. In fact they've have numerous representatives around the city come talk about it. Chairman Buie asked if there were any other agenda items for next month, and Director Couch asked to keep the scorecards on there. Chairman Buie mentioned that neither of the City Directors were present so there was no liaison feedback this month. Director Couch mentioned that he did know Director Peck, owner of Trio's which was greatly impacted by the tornado, just opened Monday. She said she wouldn't make it. This concludes the Wednesday, May 24, 2023, Park Commission Meeting. The next meeting will be Wednesday, June 14, 2023, at The Centre at University Park at noon. Buie encouraged all who could attend the following events in person. Chairman Buie thanked everyone for their reports. Meeting Adjourned.

MacArthur Military Museum The museum worked with staff from Denali Art Solutions in New Orleans to install the traveling exhibit Manufacturing Victory: The Arsenal of Democracy from the National World War II Museum in New Orleans. The exhibit, which opens to the public on May 19 and runs through September 4, follows the industrial journey that took the United States from a nation perilously unprepared for war to a global superpower that led the Allies to victory in World War II. It includes interactive touch screens, oral histories, and interpretive panels. It also includes over 30 photos from the MacArthur Museum's collection of World War II press photos from the home front. Manufacturing Victory: The Arsenal of Democracy has been on a national tour schedule sponsored by Hewett-Packard, with additional support by CITI and Motorola Solutions. Local presenting sponsors are Stephens Inc. and David F. Gruenewald. A preview reception for the new exhibit was held on May 18 and was used as a fundraiser for the museum. Approximately 125 persons attended the event. In conjunction with the exhibit opening, the museum partnered with the Clinton Presidential Center to host a presentation by Kelly Brengelman, a Kentucky Humanities living historian who portrayed Rose Leigh, the original "Rosie the Riveter" during World War II. Approximately 180 persons attended the program which was open to the public free of charge. Information on the exhibit opening and the free program were included in the Entertainment News of the Style section of the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette on Thursday, May 18. The museum's next exhibit will be to host a traveling exhibit from the Military Women's Memorial in Arlington, VA titled The Color of Freedom: Honoring the Diversity of America's Servicewomen. The exhibit will open on Saturday, June 17 and run through August 26 and is being sponsored by AARP Arkansas. Accomplishment: Had a successful opening of the new exhibit and accompanying program. He mentioned that is an important park in the city and a high profile park but that they should look at that specific park and some opportunities that they can bubble up at Parks Commission, on up to Parks and Recreation, on up to the City Director level. Chairman Buie then turned to the next agenda item, which was items for the next meeting. He called for any additional agenda items for next month. If not, then they will turn the floor over to Director Peck for feedback. Commissioner Eldridge requested they keep talking to Perry because she enjoyed his spreadsheet. Director Peck then received the floor and began by addressing the curfew. She mentioned that the board passed last night curfew for entertainment districts for youths. This was primarily requested by business owners in the River Market area specifically because in the summer months, there are more people carousing, and it appears that a lot of parents are dropping kids off at the River Market just to hang out. A couple of businesses there have closed lately, there was a threat of one major restaurant leaving if we didn't enact this curfew. That's not why we did it, but we did it for public safety purposes. The curfew is 9 pm, and it's a bad mix when there is an entertainment district where you can drink on the streets, and you have a lot of underage people that are unsupervised. That was one reason. And there's also a homeless problem that she knows everyone is aware of that is pretty aggressive, especially in the River Market. Hopefully, that will also be addressed in the next few months when the Ambassador program is launched here in the next few weeks. It extends not only to the Entertainment district but any park or pavilion that is adjacent. This is particularly targeting River Market. There were a lot of kids congregating there and getting into fights, yelling, intimidating other people. There was some board discussion that it be 10 pm. No, the kids won't be carted off to jail. They will have a citation, it will be a warning. This is an effort to make it a safe and pleasant place for all people, especially visitors and tourists that congregate in that area because we have different amenities. They have gotten no pushback that she knows of. A couple of the directors were a bit hesitant, they thought it was a bit of overreach, but 8 of them voted yes. The other big item on the agenda is that they are going back to sales tax. It may be a little premature, but she doesn't think so. It will happen, the mayor's in the process now of talking to us all individually about what they would like to see in a sales tax. The plan is to go after a full penny, this would be in November. It is heavy on Parks, he talks about the four P's. None of this has been fleshed out completely, he's getting input from them, and they plan on having 2-3 public meetings to hear what the public. The two big parks that they want to talk about are War Memorial and Hindman. The other P's are Public safety, the port, for economic reasons, and the other P is Potholes, or public works. This is not Rebuild the Rock revisited, this one is more specific, and it won't have the education or the housing piece, it will be focused on those four P's, which makes her excited because she's all about Parks! We should maybe put this as an agenda item. She mentioned that there has been talk about a sports complex in War Memorial kind of on the back side close to the interstate. Some zoo enhancements, talk about disc golf and mountain biking at Hindman as well as keeping the green space at War Memorial. It hasn't been completely fleshed out, but she expects it to ramp up here in July, with public meetings in August. She mentioned that that's a lot of information, but we can't expect our city to grow if we don't invest in it. Chairman Buie thanked Director Peck for her presentation and then accepted questions. Commissioner Ferstl clarified whether the curfew was just in entertainment districts or is there a midnight for everyone. He read somewhere that it also includes Parks. Director Peck mentioned and asked City Attorney Carpenter for assistance, but she understood it to mean it would only be a park or pavilion adjacent to an Entertainment District. Director Couch added that that was correct. Originally it was discussed to cover all City Parks. There were a lot of concerns and discussions. It was ultimately passed that any City Park that abuts an entertainment district. It's really riverfront and some of the heights and promenades. Director Peck clarified that its Selma, Heights, Hillcrest, and Riverfront. Commissioner Ferstl mentioned that he loved the idea of a sales tax and wished it would have passed the last time. He mentioned that it would be tough. Director Peck agreed that it will be tough. She mentioned that they have such a great park system and they need to take care of it. She mentioned that this is more streamlined and they learned a lot of lessons with Rebuild the Rock. It was just too much. There was a lot of grey area. She mentioned that its rare for a Park's tax to not pass, or Public Safety, or Infrastructure. These are the things that people care about the most. She is hopeful, but agrees it will take a big team effort. Commissioner Cannon Fletcher then raised his hand and mentioned that the biggest antisupporters of the last tax were the owners of the Little Rock Athletic Club and Racket Club. Is there any outreach to them to see what got them up in arms other than they don't want community centers getting better and taking their business. Director Peck mentioned that she and Commissioner Fletcher could talk about offline. She said that she honestly thinks the sales tax didn't pass not because of any one particular piece, but that it was so broad and had not been fleshed out. There were a few things that weren't under any of the P's: the affordable housing piece, the education piece, that people didn't like. She stated that if we keep it simple, the four P's, we have a much better chance. Chairman Buie then thanked Director Peck and the other Commissioners for joining. This concludes the Wednesday, June 14, 2023, Park Commission Meeting. The next meeting will be Wednesday, July 12, 2023, at The Centre at University Park at noon. Buie encouraged all who could attend the following events in person. Chairman Buie thanked everyone for their reports. Meeting Adjourned.

MacArthur Military Museum � Museum attendance for May was 2741, which was a 129% increase over last year's attendance for the month. This total includes: (1) Off-Site programming at the Therapeutic Recreation Arts Festival on May 5 and the "Rose Leigh: Rosie the Riveter" program at the Clinton Presidential Center on May 19 , (2) On-site visitation, and (3) Virtual Programming through the museum's virtual minidocumentaries and interviews. The museum hosted tours for Bald Knob High School, North Little Rock's Calvary Academy, Pulaski Tec, and STEAM for the Next Generation home school cooperative in May. The museum hosted the MacArthur Park "History on the Run" 5K race on May 5. Approximately 125 racers participated in the annual race, which is used by the Mac Park Group to raise money for MacArthur Park. This year's race raised just under $4,700 for improvements to Foster Pond. The museum continued its 2023 "Movies at MacArthur" film program with the documentary Top Secret Rosies: The Female Computers of World War II on May 30. Movies are averaging 47 persons each month in 2023, which is the highest number since the program began in 2015. The June movie, The Six Triple Eight, will be shown on June 20 in conjunction with the opening of a new traveling exhibit The Color of Freedom: Honoring the Diversity of America's Servicewomen. The film chronicles the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion which was sent to England and France in February 1945 to clear the backlog of mail in the European Theater of Operations. Known as the Six Triple Eight, it was the only all-black female battalion to serve in Europe during WWII. By war's end, the battalion had cleared over 17 million pieces of backlogged mail ensuring the troops stayed in touch with their loved ones back home. The last of the women returned home in March 1946. Movies are shown the third Tuesday of each month through November with free admission, popcorn, and beverages for all screenings. The museum opened the traveling exhibit Manufacturing Victory: The Arsenal of Democracy at a preview reception on May 18 for 125 sponsors and guests. Presenting sponsor for the exhibit, which is on loan from the National World War II Museum in New Orleans through September 4, is Stephens Inc. In conjunction with the exhibit's opening, the museum partnered with Kentucky Humanities and the Clinton Presidential Center to host a living history program "Rose Leigh: Rosie the Riveter." The program featured Kelly O'Connell Brengelman portraying Rose Leigh who was working as a riveter on B-24 bombers in Ypsilanti, Michigan in 1942 when she met actor Walter Pidgeon and appeared on the big screen as "Rosie the Riveter." Her portrayal of the iconic Rosie inspired many during World War II. Approximately 190 persons attended the free presentation in the Great Hall of the Clinton Presidential Center. The Color of Freedom: Honoring the Diversity of America's Servicewomen, a traveling exhibit from the Military Women's Memorial in Arlington, VA, will be on display at the MacArthur Museum from June 17 through August 26. Presenting sponsor for The Color of Freedom exhibit is AARP Arkansas. This exhibit tells the story of women of color who have faced barriers of gender, race and traditional cultural values in their pursuit of opportunity for service in the armed forces. From a time of segregation until now the achievements and history of these incredible women are chronicled in their fight to gain equality. Their efforts have led to a more diverse military with equal opportunities for all who now serve. Museum staff is partnering with educators from the Clinton Presidential Center to present off-site programming once again this year at the Summer Playground Program sites as well as offering on-site field trips to both museums. Staff is also planning to participate in the Little Rock School District's pilot Summer Enrichment Program in June offering off-site programming to 150 rising 3rd grade and 150 rising 4th grade students at three elementary sites � Martin Luther King, Wakefield, and Fulbright schools. Director Couch responded, the importance of graffiti removal on park property in a timely manner. Director Couch noted the areas owned by the Highway Department are handled differently. Our goal is to contact ARDOT as soon as graffiti is seen. There has been talk about creating vegetation in front of the affected areas to prevent further graffiti. Director Couch mentioned utilizing 311. 311 is a very useful tool available to the city. Chairman Buie called further questions. Director Couch had a follow-up regarding Director Lewis question about Kiwanis and Pankey parks projects. The Department is in the process of getting designs and proposals. Director Dorsey is in the process of getting neighborhood input. Director Couch is working with Sky Browner, local contact in Pankey, and getting in touch with the president of the Neighborhood Association. Director Couch mentioned staff attending a back to school event or creating a pop-up event in the park. Director Couch commented on the timeline of park projects, along with promoting them on social media. Chairman Buie thanked all who spoke for their time and efforts. Chairman Buie recognized Commissioner Ron Bara's attendance of his first meeting. Commissioner Ron Bara mentioned his reasoning behind becoming a Parks Commissioner. Old Business Chairman Buie opened the old business by asking Director Couch to mention some of upcoming events. Director Couch noted two upcoming private events War Memorial Park is to have a lifestyle medic Central Arkansas walk and Murray Park is having a bass fishing tournament. Friends of Fouche Creek will be hosting a creek cleanup. The Parks staff will be having a Pushy Plants event in Boyle Park. The Pushy Plants group is dedicated to the removal of invasive species of plants within the parks. At War Memorial, Catholic High School alumni will have a bike opening for a local chapter. Chairman Buie thanked Director Couch and encouraged the Commissioners to attend if given the availability. Chairman Buie then moved on to the next order of business: crime analysis. Director Couch responded by mentioning Mr. Courtney Perry and how appreciative Director Couch was for Mr. Perry's report last month. With new findings, Mr. Perry requested to give his final report next month. Chairman Buie also commented on Mr. Perry's report and how all are looking forward to his next report. Chairman Buie then moved on to the next order of business: scorecard analysis of park assets. Director Couch mentioned his appreciation for those who participated. Director Couch explained his intentions with the information and went over the following highlights. In the Recreation Division: pickleball, playgrounds, and new sports were all mentioned a couple of times. In the Programs Division: summer playground programs, outdoor recreation programs, and tennis. A new position with the Program Division has been opened, the Outdoor Recreation Program Coordinator. In the Facilities Division: pickleball, Murray Park river trail access, and golf. In the Community Centers: security, sport facilities, maintenance and development. We would like for our starting focus to be golf, pickleball, tennis and new sports. Under Parks: River trail, Murray, the river area, Community Centers, and playgrounds. Focusing on the playgrounds will help us advertise more on our neighborhood parks. Miscellaneous would include security, maintenance and development. Director Couch mentioned he will work with staff to finalize the information and eventually use the information to push it out to the public. Example mentioned is Rebsamen Golf Course. Director Couch appreciated everyone's input and looks forward to further discussion and ideas. Chairman Buie thanked Director Couch and called for questions. There were none. Chairman Buie then moved on to the next item of business: Golf Tournament. This item falls under the purview of Commissioner Lauren Eldridge who is absent from today's meeting. Item has been tabled. Chairman Buie then moved on to the next item of business: sub-committee reports. Chairman Buie opened the floor to Commissioner Ben France to speak on social media outreach. Commissioner France commented on how excited he is for the new Parks Marketing and Social Media Coordinator. Chairman Buie tabled the conversation due to the absence of Commissioner Lauren Eldridge, unless Director Couch had anything to mention. Director Couch had nothing to add. Commissioner France inquired about the potential candidates the department currently had for the position. Director Nelson did not have accurate information to share at the time. Chairman Buie then moved on to the next item of business within the sub-committee report, master plan. Commissioner Linda Smith updated the floor about the master plan. The subcommittee has not met due to a number of calendar conflicts. The sub-committee does plan to meet before the next commission meeting. Commissioner Smith asked if there was a limit of people available to work on a sub-committee. Chairman Buie informed all there was not a limit. City Attorney Beth Carpenter confirmed, no limit for sub-committee members. Commissioner Smith recommended adding Commissioner Mike Bernardo to the master plan sub-committee. Chairman Buie moved for a motion to add Commissioner Bernardo to the sub-committee. Commissioner Smith motioned, seconded by Commissioner Bara. Motion passed. Director Couch asked for Commissioner Smith to clarify if the committee has met before and just hasn't met recently. Commissioner Smith commented they met in January and would like to meet again. Chairman Buie then moved on to the next item of business within the sub-committee report, Parks Conservancy. Commissioner Lauren Eldridge is the Parks Conservancy liaison. In her stead Chairman Buie gave the following announcement. The Parks Conservancy has begun a public campaign. If you see the information on social media, please share to create awareness for the Parks Conservancy. The parks conservancy will have its very first event for their Friends of Parks Conservancy. More information will be available soon. Chairman Buie then began addressing New Business. New Business Chairman Buie opened the floor to Director Couch to address Fourche Creek Park. Director Couch wanted to inform the Commissioners of ideas for creating a park. Similar to that of a previous discussion about Rose Creek Park. Director Couch gave a brief history of partnership between Rose Creek Neighborhood and the Parks Department. With that being said, Fourche Creek Park has not been officially recognized as a city park. There is an official water trail on Fouche Creek, a partnership with the Arkansas Game and Fish and Friends of Fourche Creek. The Parks Department has maintained the park area. Roughly 1,800 acres with several access points available that the department would like to develop further. Director Couch then asked the Commissioners if they would support recognizing Fourche Creek as an actual city park. This would be the first step in moving forward to naming the area Fourche Creek Park. Next step would be to take the request to the City Board for approval. Chairman Buie then opened the floor to the Commissioners. Commissioner Smith inquired about the proposed boundaries of the park. Director Couch mentioned the zoning of PR. The boundaries considered for the park would be those zoned for PR. Exact boundaries as of this meeting were not available. Commissioner Smith followed up with a question about if the Parks Department was currently maintaining the area mentioned. Director Couch mentioned the natural swamp bottom area that is Fouche Creek. Due to the terrain there are cleanups to maintain the area, but the resources to collect all the trash are not currently available. Multiple City Parks abut to the creek already. Along with several different trails both current and future development. Commissioner Smith followed up with a question regarding structural plans for the proposed park. Director Couch mentioned there will not be any additional structures at this point. There is potential discussion about a future stand-alone area for the "entrance" to Fouche Creek Park. Chairman Buie called for any further questions or further discussion. Commissioner Mike Bernardo mentioned he was unfamiliar with Fourche. He questioned Director Couch about what criteria makes a parcel of land usable for a city park. Director Couch mentioned the city is already maintaining and making plans in the Fourche Creek area. Director Couch believes it is important to recognize the area as an official city park. There is already the mentality that the area is being used as a park. The choosing of park land is a whole different conversation. Chairman Buie recognized Director Peck. Director Peck mentioned she along with others already assumed the area was a city park. Fourche Creek is such an important area geographically because of the watershed, trails and Gillam Park. Along with the multiple partners involved in the conservation easement. Director Peck mentioned a group was interested in filming in the area for a new Indiana Jones film, using the Cyprus trees. Director Peck mentions several reasons why the City should recognize the Fourche Creek area as an official park. Director Couch thanked Director Peck commented on the nature and wildlife aspects of the area he had yet to mention, minus all the trash. Director Couch mentioned floating of Fourche Creek on August 7, 2023. The creek is the city's biggest watershed and flood plain. Due to the sudden flow of water, building of structures would be a hassle. Chairman Buie called for any final questions or further discussion. There were none. Chairman Buie called for a motion of the naming of Fourche Creek Park as an official City park. Commissioner Samuel Ellis motioned, seconded by Commissioner Ben France. Motion carried. Chairman Buie then moved on to the next item of business mentioning he believed the Commission has already spoken on the golf tournament and scorecard analysis. If further discussion was needed, Director Couch would let the floor know. There was no further discussion needed. Chairman Buie called for agenda items for next meeting. There were none. Chairman Buie recognized Director Peck had to leave the meeting early. He then dedicated the last five (5) board liaison feedback. Opening the floor to Director Lewis. Director Lewis was thankful for the updates received and looking forward to taking information back to share with the public. This concludes the Wednesday, July 12, 2023, Park Commission Meeting. The next meeting will be Wednesday, August 9, 2023, at The Centre at University Park at noon. Buie encouraged all who could attend the following events in person. Chairman Buie thanked everyone for their reports. Chairman Buie thanked Commissioners and others for joining. Meeting Adjourned, 12:56pm.
